articles.title: A.J. Brown's knee report takes unexpected turn as $25 million payment dispute raises fresh questions about his exit
articles.summary: New England Patriots are still waiting for A.J.
articles.body: New England Patriots are still waiting for A.J. Brown to make a meaningful impact, but head coach Mike Vrabel has offered a different explanation for why the wide receiver left Tennessee in 2022. Asked whether the Titans had concerns about Brown's knees before trading him, Vrabel pointed to a contract dispute involving the franchise's ownership. His comments have brought the $25 million annual figure back into focus and raised fresh questions about the decisions behind Brown's departure from Tennessee.Mike Vrabel points to money behind A.J. Brown's Titans exitVrabel addressed the subject during an appearance on WEEI's "The Greg Hill Show" on Monday. The question referred to a report claiming doctors had warned Tennessee's leadership in 2022 that Brown's knee had only two years left.It also asked whether that medical assessment influenced the ownership's decision to trade him and whether Vrabel knew about the concerns at the time.The Patriots coach did not accept that explanation. Instead, he pointed directly to the financial disagreement that surrounded Brown's contract situation.“No, the owner didn’t want to pay A.J. Brown 25 million dollars,” Vrabel said. “That’s what it was.”Vrabel also brought up Brown's availability during his time with the Philadelphia Eagles, suggesting that his injury history did not tell the complete story behind Tennessee's decision.“He went to Philly, and I mean, A.J. has participated in quite a handful of games; and has missed a few since he went to Philly,” Vrabel said.The Titans traded Brown to Philadelphia during the 2022 NFL Draft. In return, Tennessee received the 18th and 101st overall picks. Brown then signed a four-year, $100 million extension with the Eagles, putting his average annual salary at $25 million.His production offered little reason to question the move from Philadelphia's perspective. Brown recorded more than 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first four seasons with the Eagles. He also played all 17 regular-season games in both 2022 and 2023, before appearing in 13 games in 2024 and 15 in 2025.Patriots still waiting for Brown to deliver after tradeVrabel now has Brown in New England, but the early returns have been far from what the Patriots hoped to get from the receiver. The franchise acquired him on June 1, sending a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick to Philadelphia.Brown has managed just 11 receptions for 128 yards and no touchdowns across four games. His latest outing against the Detroit Lions brought only two catches for 27 yards.That production is a concern for a Patriots team that invested significant draft capital to bring him in. However, Vrabel suggested that Brown's current struggles were not something the coaching staff expected after watching him during the summer.“But by all indications, unfortunately, after the training camp that he had, I wouldn’t have anticipated anything,” he said.The coach also described the setbacks Brown has faced, including getting rolled up on during the season opener and being dragged down during his latest injury incident.Vrabel did not offer a timeline for his return. The Patriots will have to wait until Brown is healthy enough to contribute again.“So we’ll just keep trying to get him healthy and whenever he can get back out there to help us, I know that he will.”For Vrabel, the current priority is getting Brown back on the field. But his comments have also reopened an old debate about whether Tennessee's decision was driven by concerns over his knees or an unwillingness to meet his contract demands.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 12: Latest news, updates for Kenneth Walker III, Brock Bowers, more players for fantasy football
articles.summary: It's Thanksgiving week and there are games on five different days. We're updating you on the latest NFL injuries for fantasy football.
articles.body:
It's Thanksgiving week in the NFL and there's a lot to go over, both on the injury front and the schedule. The Packers and Rams play Wednesday night, while we have the usual three-game Thanksgiving lineup. We also have the Broncos and Steelers on Black Friday, then the normal Sunday slate and Monday Night Football.

So Week 12 is spread across five different days, which can be pretty hectic for fantasy football managers. We're here to help out, taking you through the NFL injury report with the latest updates and some fantasy analysis for key players.

Justin Herbert, LAC (concussion protocol)

Drake Maye, NE (leg) — Out at least six weeks

Herbert : The Chargers have shown signs of life over the past two weeks, scoring 23 and 24 points, respectively. Herbert turned in his first QB1 finish of the 2026 season with 22.44 fantasy points against the Jets on Sunday. He only had 131 passing yards, two TDs, 32 rushing yards and another score on the ground, so it isn't like "we are so back" or anything. But now Herbert will need to clear concussion protocol in order to play Week 12 against the Patriots, another solid matchup.

With how the QB landscape is right now, if Herbert can clear, he isn't a bad add as a QB2 or streaming option for Week 12. The Chargers have some winnable matchups down the stretch and Herbert will likely need to throw. Maybe Herbert and the Chargers can still salvage something for fantasy.

Darnold : The reigning Super Bowl champ has missed the past two games but has a shot to get back on the field for Week 12 against the 49ers in a big spot. Seattle is coming off its bye and Drew Lock has been the starter. He's been more than serviceable, undefeated in essentially four starts this season. There's not much difference between Darnold and Lock starting for fantasy managers. Whoever starts will be a QB2 this week, and either way, Jaxon Smith-Njigba will get fed.

Josh Jacobs, GB (finger) — Unlikely to play in Week 12

Walker : The Chiefs' lead back missed his second straight game Sunday, though the team didn't miss him much. Kansas City rolled to another easy win over the Cardinals, 34-7. Emmett Johnson led the backfield again with another strong performance, racking up 143 total yards, four catches and a score for 22.3 fantasy points. Johnson has RB1 finishes in three of his past four games.

The Chiefs take on the Bills in a highly anticipated matchup on Thanksgiving night. Walker will have a short week to get ready to return, which isn't ideal. If Walker sits again, Johnson can be fired up as an RB1 in what should be a high-scoring affair. If Walker is able to play, we could see him eased back into action given how well Johnson has fared in his stead. In that scenario, Walker would return to RB1/2 status while Johnson would hold value as a flex play.

Tuten : The Jaguars took a tough loss in Week 11 to the Giants and lost Tuten late in the game with an undisclosed injury. He had been dealing with an ankle issue coming into the contest, so it could have something to do with that. Either way, Tuten has been playing pretty banged up over the last handful of games.

If Tuten ends up missing Week 12, Chris Rodriguez Jr. would likely take over the backfield. He had four carries for 28 yards against New York, and has four rushing TDs on the season. C-Rod would basically be elevated to RB2 status with a matchup against the Titans in Week 12. If Tuten is active, you have to play him but know there's some risk given the injuries.

Davante Adams, LAR (hamstring) — Out until at least Week 13

Bowers : The Raiders were without their top offensive weapon for a loss to the Broncos on Sunday afternoon in Week 11. It felt like a long shot for Bowers to be ready but there's optimism he'll be back for Week 12 against the Browns. Fernando Mendoza looked better in his second NFL start, which is encouraging for Bowers' fantasy prospects. If Bowers is active, you're playing him. If he's out, there aren't any teams on bye, so there should be plenty of streaming options, including Michael Mayer, though he was quiet with just one catch for four yards on Sunday.

Kincaid : It's been another up-and-down, injury-impacted campaign for the Bills' tight end. He missed his first game of the season in Week 11 against the Dolphins but had been popping up on the injury report most weeks. Since his hot start, Kincaid only had one game with double-digit fantasy points in the past seven games. Dawson Knox got a few catches against Miami but isn't really a viable streaming option if Kincaid is out again for Thursday night's game against the Chiefs.

articles.title: ‘Tyreek Hill’s back’ – Kansas City Chiefs breakout star reminds me of former wide receiver, says Mike Florio
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ offense has stepped up a level over the past two weeks, with Patrick Mahomes throwing eight touchdown passes. The running game has al...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs' offense has stepped up a level over the past two weeks, with Patrick Mahomes throwing eight touchdown passes.

The running game has also had a different look, rookie Emmett Johnson has stepped into the backfield with Kenneth Walker dealing with an injury.

Johnson had 105 rushing yards in Week 11 and one touchdown, plus a further 38 receiving yards from four targets.

The rookie wears the Chiefs' number 10 jersey once worn by wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and Mike Florio sees similarities with his burst of pace.

Speaking to Pro Football Talk, Florio explained: "You've got to use him. I mean, people see that number 10, and I've heard people say it's Isiah Pacheco.

"When I see him running in the open field, I'm thinking Tyreek Hill's back, it is just the weirdest thing to see.

"But he is extremely effective, and there are teams out there kicking themselves that they didn't draft him when they could."

How Johnson's 40 yard dash compares to Tyreek Hill

Tyreek Hill was also a fifth-round draft pick for the Kansas City Chiefs, 10 years earlier. He went on to win one Super Bowl with Patrick Mahomes, before forcing an exit to sign with the Miami Dolphins.

Hill, 32, is attempting to recover from a serious knee injury and wants to revive his NFL career.

He was renowned as the fastest player in the NFL, and Florio's comparison is a major compliment for Emmett Johnson and his own ability to run into space with the ball.

Tyreek Hill did not participate at the NFL Combine, but set a 4.29 time at the 40-yard dash at his West Alabama Pro Day.

Emmett Johnson's dash time was an unimpressive 4.56 seconds, which also helps to explain why he fell to the fifth round.

The Chiefs still saw something special in him, and Johnson is proving it on the field where it really matters.

articles.title: "Just having that camera on me at all times": Travis Kelce revealed the surprising role Donna Kelce's home videos played in building his confidence
articles.summary: Travis Kelce's confidence in front of millions of people did not develop overnight.
articles.body: Travis Kelce's confidence in front of millions of people did not develop overnight. Long before the Kansas City Chiefs star became a familiar face on television, he had an unexpected advantage at home. His mother, Donna Kelce, loved recording family moments, and those childhood videos helped him become comfortable around cameras. During a press conference on February 2, 2024, ahead of Super Bowl LVIII, Travis opened up about how Donna's simple habit influenced his personality and why sports eventually helped him overcome his childhood shyness.How Donna Kelce's home videos helped Travis build confidenceWhen reporters asked Travis Kelce about his ease in front of cameras, he immediately credited his mother. Rather than pointing to his NFL career or years of media training, the tight end looked back at his childhood."My mom’s home videos, man," Travis said during the February 2, 2024 press conference.He explained that Donna frequently recorded him while he was growing up, making cameras a familiar part of his everyday life."Just having that camera on me at all times, seeing what silly stuff I'm gonna do next, man," he added.The experience appeared to remove some of the discomfort that many people feel when they are being filmed. Travis said he had always felt comfortable in different settings and found it easy to look into a camera."Honestly, I've always been comfortable in the rooms that I've been in and just been fortunate that I've been able to kind of look into a camera with ease, I guess."For Donna, recording her children was a way to preserve family memories. However, those videos also gave Travis years of exposure to cameras before his professional career brought constant public attention.Travis Kelce revealed how sports helped him overcome childhood shynessInterestingly, Travis did not credit home videos alone for shaping his confidence. He also spoke about how playing sports helped him become more expressive.Despite his outgoing personality today, the NFL star admitted that he was quite different as a child."You probably won't believe it, but I was a shy kid growing up until I got onto the sports field or the court or the ice rink," he explained.According to Travis, competing gave him an environment where he could relax, enjoy himself and show more of his personality. Success on the field gradually strengthened his belief in himself."I was having success, and that just kind of propelled me to have confidence in life," he said.Those experiences became particularly relevant as his career expanded beyond football. From hosting Saturday Night Live in March 2023 to appearing in television commercials and entertainment projects, Travis embraced opportunities that placed him in front of new audiences.His February 2024 admission offered an interesting reminder that the personality fans now recognise had developed through years of small experiences. Donna's home videos and his love for sports both played a part in that journey.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From a $200 signing deal to a $3.1 million auction record: How Tom Brady's rookie card became a collector's treasure
articles.summary: Tom Brady's legendary NFL career eventually turned him into one of the most valuable names in sports memorabilia.
articles.body: Tom Brady's legendary NFL career eventually turned him into one of the most valuable names in sports memorabilia. But his first trading card deal was hardly a million-dollar opportunity. When the future seven-time Super Bowl champion entered the league as the 199th overall pick in 2000, he was happy to earn a few hundred dollars for signing cards. More than two decades later, those same signatures became highly sought-after collectibles. In 2021, two copies of his rookie card made auction history, with one fetching more than $3.1 million.Tom Brady's $200 rookie card deal became a million-dollar collectibleBefore becoming an NFL icon, Tom Brady had little reason to imagine that his signature would one day command millions. His agent, Steve, brought him a trading card opportunity early in his career. The offer involved signing 1,000 cards for 20 cents each.Brady recalled the conversation during an appearance on Good Morning America in April 2021.“My agent, Steve, was like, ‘Got a trading card deal for you. You sign a thousand cards and they’re gonna pay you like 20 cents a card,'” Brady said. “Twenty cents a card? I’m gonna be rich!”The arrangement earned him just $200. However, the value of his autograph changed dramatically as his career took off. By 2021, Brady had won seven Super Bowls, including his first championship with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Collectors were also spending record amounts on rare football cards.A copy of his 2000 Playoff Contenders Championship Rookie Ticket autograph card sold for $1.32 million in March 2021. Fitbit CEO James Park purchased that edition, but another sale soon pushed the record much higher.Tom Brady rookie card shattered auction records in 2021On April 2, 2021, Lelands auctioned another copy of the same card, numbered 99 out of just 100 produced. The card had spent years in a private collection after being purchased on eBay more than a decade earlier.Bidding opened at $75,000. After 67 bids, an anonymous buyer paid $2,252,854, setting a new public auction record for a football card.Another collector, who owned a copy he believed was in better condition, saw an opportunity to surpass that figure.Lelands director of acquisitions Jordan Gilroy explained the buyer's motivation to The Washington Times.“He wanted to use the momentum of us setting that initial world record and essentially break it,” Gilroy said.The strategy worked. On June 4, 2021, the collector's card sold for $3,107,372 at Lelands' Mid-Spring Classic. Beckett graded it Mint 9, while its autograph received a perfect 10.Although a one-of-one Patrick Mahomes card reportedly fetched $4.3 million in a private sale later, Brady's June 2021 transaction remained a landmark public auction result.For Brady, those early $200 earnings became a remarkable reminder of how much his name and signature had grown in value.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Packers star Micah Parsons reportedly cleared to return from ACL injury, will make season debut vs. Rams on Thanksgiving Eve
articles.summary: Micah Parsons has been recovering from a torn ACL and meniscus in his left knee for nearly a full year.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers star pass rusher has been cleared to return and will make his season debut in their Thanksgiving Eve matchup with the Los Angeles Rams, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

It will mark Parsons' first NFL game since he tore his left ACL and meniscus last season. He went down with the knee injury in their loss to the Denver Broncos on Dec. 14 , and has been sidelined recovering ever since. The Packers lost four straight games after losing Parsons, including a playoff loss to the Chicago Bears.

Parsons had 12.5 sacks in his 14 games with the Packers last season, and had accounted for a third of Green Bay's pressures before he went down. It was his first campaign with the team after they acquired him in a deal with the Dallas Cowboys just ahead of Week 1.

Parsons was cleared to return to practice earlier this month and started his ramp-up while targeting Wednesday's game at SoFi Stadium for his return. Clearly, that has gone exactly to plan.

"I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday, but for sure this season," Parsons said on Monday afternoon before meeting with team doctors, via The Athletic's Matt Schneidman . "I'll be looking forward to returning to the field."

The Packers will enter Wednesday with a 6-4 record, which has them in last in the NFC North but very much alive in the playoff conversation. They were off last week, but went into their bye fresh off a rough 30-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

While it's been almost a full year since he's played in a game, Parsons is more than ready to get back. And he's well aware of what a win over the Rams would do for the Packers' postseason hopes entering the final stretch of the season.

"I'm really geeked up," he said, via ESPN's Rob Demovsky. "They're like, 'Are you nervous?' I'm just so focused, I'm so locked in on what's ahead of me. I understand what this game Wednesday means to the organization, myself and what it means for playoffs. If I can be out there, I want to be out there."

articles.title: Tom Brady Admits He’s Made Parenting ‘Mistakes’: ‘I Threw a Lot of Interceptions’
articles.summary: “I’d hope I’m a better parent today than I was when I first started having kids,” the father of three said
articles.body:
Tom Brady appeared on the Sunday, Nov. 22, episode of the High Performance podcast, where he briefly opened up about parenting his three kids

The retired NFL star shares son John "Jack", 19, with ex-girlfriend Bridget Moynahan, and son Benjamin, 16, and daughter Vivian, 13, with ex-wife Gisele Bündchen

He confessed that he's "tried to learn from" each parenting mistake he's made

Tom Brady admitted he's always striving to be a "better" dad to his three kids .

The retired NFL quarterback, 49, appeared on the Sunday, Nov. 22 episode of Jake Humphrey's High Performance podcast, where he opened up about parenting his three kids. Brady shares son John "Jack" , 19, with ex-girlfriend Bridget Moynahan , and 16-year-old son Benjamin Rein and 13-year-old daughter Vivian Lake with ex-wife Gisele Bündchen .

Brady said he makes a deliberate effort to show his children he wants to learn what they value.

"The important thing for me in my personal life is to go where my kids are at too," he explained. "I think it's been a really important lesson for me over the years to go to my kids and say, what's really important to you, what's driving you, or what are you scared of, or how can I pay attention to the things that you value?"

Brady continued, "So part of that is just being really open and present and also trying to be really relatable to the younger [generation], which I was very fortunate to learn over the course of my playing career."

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

Humphrey commended the athlete for his parenting advice, saying he'd listen to a podcast called Parenting Tips with Tom Brady .

However, Brady noted, "Well, I've made a lot of mistakes."

"So, a lot like quarterback. I threw a lot of interceptions. And [at] every one I've tried to learn from," he said. "And I'd hope I'm a better parent today than I was when I first started having kids. And hopefully I'm a better parent 10 years from now."

He also opened up about teaching his children to build resilience, explaining that he's really "doubled down" on "not letting them off the hook with the lessons they need to learn," particularly in the last two years.

The father of three said he's "trying to really be a mentor to them."

Mentoring his children sometimes resembles how he mentored teammates, Brady said.

"My son said to me the other night, he's like, 'Dad, sometimes we sit down at dinner, and it's just like a really easy conversation to start, and all of a sudden you get really serious, Dad,' " Brady explained. "And I'm like, 'You're right, Benny. Sometimes I do, sometimes that coach comes out in me.' "

"You know I'm taking these things that they're giving to me and their lessons from their day, and then I'm trying to say, 'Okay, well, you're 16 years old. I'm a little bit older than you. I was 16; I remember that this is what I would do, based on the 30-plus years of experience that I have.' "

The five-time Super Bowl MVP said he tries to be "really present" and "non-judgmental" with his kids. "Just trying to understand their perspective, but also trying to get them to understand my perspective a little bit too."

articles.title: David Bailey already drawing Hall of Fame comparison 10 games into Jets career
articles.summary: Davis said Bailey has only scratched the surface of what he can do.
articles.body:
Demario Davis is in his 15th NFL season, and he has played with some greats.

The Jets linebacker sees traits in rookie edge rusher David Bailey that he has observed in some of those great ones. Davis praised Bailey's "process" on Monday, saying the rookie does not let outside factors affect his preparation routine, similarly to the best players he has been around.

"I don't know what all goes into his process, but I know I see him in the same spots around the building all the time," Davis said. "That type of stuff is what I've seen from guys who are now in the Hall of Fame. When you come in and you go through the week, you see them in the same spots in the building all the time, whether it was an All-Pro wide receiver or an All-Pro running back or an All-Pro quarterback, an All-Pro defensive end in Cam Jordan — a solidified Hall of Famer, one of the best I've ever seen do it — it's all about that process. Those guys have a regimen and a routine that doesn't change based on what's going on around them. That's very rare to see for a rookie."

Bailey has been a star on the field. He added two sacks against the Chargers to bring his season total to 9 ½, just shy of Hugh Douglas' Jets rookie record of 10 set in 1995. He is five away from Jevon Kearse's NFL rookie record of 14 ½, established in 1999.

Davis said Bailey has only scratched the surface of what he can do.

"He's only going to get better," the veteran linebacker said. "It's going to be scary for a lot of quarterbacks for a long time and it's going to be good for the Jets for a long time."

The Jets gave up a touchdown just before halftime Sunday when Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert ran for a 10-yard score as time expired. The Jets showed an interesting defense on the play, with three players rushing and eight players lined up on the goal line. Herbert took off, and the Jets could not bring him down. If they had tackled him, the Chargers might have been unable to even kick a field goal. Both Dane Belton and Davis missed tackles on the play.

"They had a chance to try to score on a throwing play and we had guys in the end zone," head coach Aaron Glenn said, "but then again, if he had a chance to run it, we had guys able to converge on the ball and I think if you look at that play, I think we had two missed tackles, which would've put them in a tough situation with six seconds to try to run the ball in that situation. The thing is we just got to make that tackle. We make that tackle; we put ourselves in a good position."

articles.title: Dan Orlovsky stumped by Mina Kimes’ Alamo reference
articles.summary: Dan Orlovsky is an NFL analyst across ESPN platforms, most prominently on the award-winning NFL Live. He’s also a professional oversharer. Orlovsky has made...
articles.body:
Dan Orlovsky is an NFL analyst across ESPN platforms, most prominently on the award-winning NFL Live . He's also a professional oversharer.

Orlovsky has made a habit out of captivating the nation with his unique habits , leading to a bland grilled chicken birthday cake , and his character arc regarding pedicures .

Just in the past month, Orlovsky asked The Pat McAfee Show crew whether it's possible to walk from Alaska to Russia, declared himself a non-smoker (and threw his poor wife under the bus) on NFL Live , and learned live on national television what percent means.

Now, the history of the Alamo isn't common knowledge like the definition of percent, but it also flew over Orlovsky's head.

On Sunday, Orlovsky tweeted , "The Texans are alive." On Monday, Mina Kimes, Orlovsky's NFL Live colleague, reposted it and quipped , "General Santa Anna on the morning of March 6, 1836."

Orlovsky replied, "Wtf this mean," and Kimes had the perfect meme prepared to put a bow on this whole exchange:

Leave it to Kimes, recent champion of Celebrity Jeopardy! All Stars , to turn Orlovsky's very basic Houston Texans tweet into a history lesson on Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna and the Texas Revolution.

It is always possible that Orlovsky was joking, but given his track record of earnest unawareness, it's more likely that Kimes' joke flew over his head. But honestly, in a sports media landscape littered with know-it-alls, we would all be better off if more people were willing to simply ask, "Wtf this mean."

articles.title: Bengals safety Bryan Cook injures ankle vs Commanders Monday night
articles.summary: Bengals safety Bryan Cook hurt his ankle during the team's NFL Week 11 game against Washington on Monday night.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals safety Bryan Cook injured his right ankle during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 11 game against the Washington Commanders on ESPN's Monday Night Football at Northwest Stadium.

Cook walked off the field to the sideline under his own power.

The Bengals announced that Cook's return is questionable.

"It looked like it was gonna be a lot worse," MNF analyst Troy Aikman said during the broadcast. "Definitely a good sign to see him walking off (the field)."

Cook was hurt after he was in on a sack of Ravens quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley during the team's NFL Week 7 rout in Baltimore. Cook got up and walked slowly off the field, and returned to the game later in the fourth quarter.

Cook hurt his ankle during the first quarter of the team's NFL Week 3 loss in Pittsburgh. Cook missed two games because of the injury.

See photos from Bengals vs. Commanders on Monday Night Football

Cook, a former Mount Healthy High School standout and Cincinnati Bearcats defensive back, was on the sideline after having his ankle taped during the Steelers' second scoring drive of the game. Cook returned to the game early in the second quarter.

Cook agreed to terms March 9 on a reported three-year deal worth $40.25 million.

"My family's been talking about this for a long time," Cook said March 12. "Being able to come back home and … be closer to our family. I'm just excited for the opportunity, excited for the new chapter in my life."

Cook was at Kansas City's T-Mobile Center to watch the ninth-seeded Bearcats ' men's basketball team defeat No. 16 seed Utah in the Big 12 tournament.

Cook starred at UC from 2019 to 2021 before becoming a second-round pick of the Chiefs in 2022.

articles.body:
While the fans at Northwest Stadium did their best with cell-phone lights, it didn't exactly do the trick during Monday's game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders when the lights went out.

And that is exactly what happened in the third quarter with the Commanders driving deep in Cincinnati territory:

Fortunately for both teams and the fans, the lights were out for approximately two minutes. It wasn't a lengthy delay, and Washington continued the drive that ended with a made field goal.

The lights also temporarily went out during their Week 9 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Spain.

At least the lights haven't gone out during any of their home games this season.

articles.title: Sam Darnold Injured, Latest on Seahawks QB vs. 49ers and Everything HC Macdonald Said About Recovery
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald wants to see how quarterback Sam Darnold looks during practice on Wednesday before making a final decision about his status for Sunday's divisional matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, according to ESPN's Brady Henderson.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald wants to see how quarterback Sam Darnold looks during practice on Wednesday before making a final decision about his status for Sunday's divisional matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, according to ESPN's Brady Henderson .

The 29-year-old has missed the past two games with a quadriceps injury and a cracked rib , both of which he suffered during a loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8. Macdonald told reporters on Monday that Darnold made "a good bit of progress" over the past week, according to Henderson.

"He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here," Macdonald said, per Henderson. "He also was able to get away. He's optimistic, but I think just with today's practice cadence and speed today, I think it's probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday's practice."

Darnold returned to practice on Monday, but the team did not hold a full-speed practice, according to Seahawks reporter John Boyle .

"He looked great," McDonald said, per Henderson. "Everything was positive today. He took a ton of reps, but it wasn't a full-speed -- it was more of a [walk-through] tempo."

The Seahawks have found success with backup quarterback Drew Lock when Darnold has been forced to miss time this season.

Darnold's storybook season in 2025 culminated with Seattle winning its second Super Bowl in franchise history, but his 2026 campaign has been marred by injuries.

Darnold missed nearly the entirety of the Seahawks' regular-season opener after suffering a glute injury on the fifth play of the game, and Lock stepped in to lead Seattle to a narrow 13-10 victory. Lock got his first start of the season in Week 2, and he put together a three-touchdown performance as the Seahawks routed the Arizona Cardinals.

Darnold returned to action in Week 3, but he threw nine interceptions over the next six games . When the veteran quarterback's latest injury earned Lock another start in Week 10, the backup stepped in and dazzled once again.

Lock has led Seattle to a spotless 4-0 record while throwing seven touchdowns with zero interceptions, but Macdonald quickly shut down any potential whispers of a brewing quarterback controversy.

"Drew's been fantastic," Macdonald said last Monday on Seattle Sports 710-AM, per Henderson . "He's been phenomenal, but Sam's our quarterback."

Darnold has evidently earned the benefit of the doubt, but he has also faced far tougher opponents than his backup. In Lock's three starts — two against the Cardinals and one against the Raiders — he has faced the two worst-ranked scoring defenses in the league, per Pro Football Reference .

The Seahawks hold a 6-4 record heading into their Week 12 tilt against San Francisco.

articles.title: Mystery solved: Here's why the 'Monday Night Football' lights went out on Bengals-Commanders
articles.summary: As it turns out, someone simply forgot to disable the regular weekday timer at Northwest Stadium.
articles.body:
Someone at Northwest Stadium made a simple, critical error on Monday night.

They forgot the Washington Commanders were playing on a weekday.

Power suddenly went out early in the second half of the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday. Just before the Commanders were set to snap the ball, everything went dark — which elicited a loud reaction from fans at the stadium in Maryland.

Thankfully, the issue didn't take long to sort out. ESPN went to a commercial, the lights were turned back on and the game continued on normally. It was nothing like the power outage that occurred during Super Bowl XLVII in 2013, which halted play for more than a half hour in New Orleans.

The issue Monday night wasn't a technical one by any means. As it turns out, according to ESPN's Joe Buck, the lighting vendor didn't disable the regularly scheduled 10 p.m. switch that shuts the lights off at the stadium during the week.

"It's a weekday thing, and they forgot it was a Monday night game," Buck said.

That's a mistake rarely seen at even the college level, let alone the professional ranks. Brutal.

In the vendor's defense, this is the first time this season the Commanders have hosted a game on a day other than Sunday. They played on the road against the San Francisco 49ers on a Monday night in Week 6, and they were at the New York Giants on Thursday night last week.

But with a primetime game on deck, ensuring that the lights stay on feels like it would be one of the first things that gets checked.

Unless one of the Commanders' final three games of the season gets flexed to Monday night, this will be their last weekday primetime game of the season. While their move to their new stadium in D.C. is still a few years off — the Commanders are targeting a 2030 move — hopefully the vendor makes note of the Northwest Stadium maintenance switch for next season after Monday night's error.

articles.title: Commanders Shock Bengals, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Burrow, Daniels, Chase, Top Players
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders upset the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday after a stunning final drive and a walk-off field goal.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders upset the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday after a stunning final drive and a walk-off field goal.

The Bengals led by one point with just 46 seconds remaining, but Jayden Daniels led the offense down the field, and kicker Drew Stevens won it with a field goal.

Daniels After Win: 'I Live for These Moments'

The rainy weather in Washington made for a slow start for both offenses. The game started with four consecutive punts and a turnover on downs for the Bengals.

Cincinnati finally got on the board first in the second quarter with a field goal. On the next offensive drive for the Bengals, Samaje Perine made a big play to move the ball down the field before Joe Burrow found Tee Higgins for a touchdown to make it 10-0.

The Commanders answered on the following drive, however, as Jayden Daniels led the offense down the field and Jacory Croskey-Merritt punched it in on the goal line.

Washington tied things up with a field goal to start the third quarter, but the Bengals quickly regained the lead thanks to a touchdown pass from Burrow to Colbie Young.

The Commanders answered the score with a field goal before getting another to start the fourth, cutting the lead to just one point. Washington then forced a Bengals punt and took the lead on the following drive with another field goal, leaving Cincinnati with just over two minutes to respond.

Burrow quickly got to work, finding Higgins on a 12-yard pass before getting into field goal range with a 32-yard pass to Mike Gesicki.

Burrow then nearly threw an interception that would have sealed the game for the Commanders, but Rasul Douglas couldn't hang on to it.

He took a sack on third down that moved the ball back to the 38-yard-line, but kicker Evan McPherson's 56-yarder was still true, and the Commanders had 46 seconds to answer.

The Commanders have struggled in late-game situations this year, but didn't mess up this time. After the kickoff, Daniels found Antonio Williams to get the ball to the 50-yard line before finding Williams again, this time a 42-yard pass that set up the field goal.

Even with the win, it's fair to say that every game moving forward is a must-win for the Commanders. The New York Giants continue to improve their stronghold in the NFC East, and a rough start for Washington means it can't afford anymore losses.

The Bengals, meanwhile, are still in control in the AFC East, but still have to keep their foot on the gas with the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers not far behind them.

articles.title: NFL Playoff Bracket Scenarios 2026-27 Week 12 Updated After Bengals Upset by Commanders
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders kept their playoff hopes alive with a stunning upset of the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders kept their playoff hopes alive with a stunning upset of the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night.

Washington moved to 4-5-1 and is two games back of the New York Giants in the NFC East.

The Commanders have a favorable upcoming schedule, so there's a good chance they can at least put pressure on the Giants and the Dallas Cowboys in the coming weeks in the NFC East.

As for the Bengals, Monday's loss dropped them behind the Jacksonville Jaguars in the top four of the AFC standings.

Cincinnati should recover from the loss in Week 12, but it has a few difficult games ahead that could knock it from the top of the AFC North.

Cincinnati's last-second loss to Washington dropped it behind the Jacksonville Jaguars and down to the No. 4 seed.

Jacksonville owns a head-to-head win over the Bengals from Week 4 that could turn out to be a vital result in the playoff standings when the regular season is finished.

That could be the difference between playing the Kansas City Chiefs, who are currently the No. 5 seed, and the Cleveland Browns, the current No. 6 seed.

The Bengals will see the Browns twice in Weeks 13 and 18 in games that will likely decide the AFC North title.

Joe Burrow and Co. should recover fine in Week 12 at home against the New Orleans Saints, but then they face a brutal two-game stretch against the Browns and Chiefs.

Looking ahead to Week 12, the Buffalo Bills host Chiefs in what many will call an AFC Championship Game preview because of the long history between Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes.

A Kansas City win would bring Buffalo back to the pack and congest the race for home-field advantage.

That's the result the Bengals have to be rooting for after their missed opportunity on Monday.

Monday's win does gives the Commanders some confidence that they can chase down a playoff spot.

The Commanders need a lot of help to get from 4-5-1 to the top of the NFC East, but they have a path to attempt to get there. They visit the Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans in the next two weeks. Both of those are winnable games.

They still need the New York Giants and Dallas Cowboys to lose some games, but at least Washington has a fighting chance going into Week 12.

The NFC playoff picture will be under the spotlight throughout Week 12, starting on Wednesday night, when the Green Bay Packers visit the Los Angeles Rams.

The Chicago Bears visit the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day to decide first place in the NFC North.

On Sunday, the San Francisco 49ers play host to the Seattle Seahawks in a game that's massive for the reigning Super Bowl champion to pull itself back into the NFC West title race.

articles.title: Watch Joe Burrow, Jayden Daniels Embrace on Video After Commanders' Stunning Upset of Bengals
articles.summary: One LSU quarterback got the best of the other during Monday night's game, but it was still nothing but love for the two Tigers in the aftermath.
articles.body:
One LSU quarterback got the best of the other during Monday night's game, but it was still nothing but love for the two Tigers in the aftermath.

After leading his Washington Commanders to a 22-20 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals, Jayden Daniels embraced Joe Burrow on the field:

Daniels After Win: 'I Live for These Moments'

It looked as if Burrow led the Bengals on a game-winning drive when he put them in position for Evan McPherson to drill a 56-yard go-ahead field goal in the final minute.

However, that left enough time on the clock for Daniels to play hero.

And he did just that with two long completions to Antonio Williams, the second of which set up a chip-shot 26-yard field goal from Drew Stevens to clinch the win for Washington and snap Cincinnati's five-game winning streak.

articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 12: Is it time to start taking the Giants seriously?
articles.summary: The Giants' upset win over the Jaguars changes things. It boosts their chances of making the playoffs as a division champion.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

Before Week 11, the New York Giants had a perception problem.

They hadn't beaten a team with a winning record. Their advanced metrics said they were a below-average team. Their point differential was +7, which was meager for a 5-3-1 team. They looked like a team lucky to be playing in the putrid NFC East.

Then on Sunday, the Giants got a win that can help legitimize their start . They beat a Jaguars team that was a major buyer at the trade deadline and looked like one of the NFL's elite teams . It was easily the Giants' biggest win this season, and for a team that has missed the playoffs eight of the past nine seasons, one of their biggest victories in many years. It might change what is being said about the Giants.

"We don't really worry about that, we don't really care what they think or what they say," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the game, via the team's transcripts. "It's not our concern how we're evaluated. It's our concern how we play."

Yet, they knew what was being said about them.

"They keep saying we can't beat these teams, we can't beat them. I don't know why they're saying that," edge rusher Abdul Carter said, according to Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein . "But what are they going to say now?"

The Giants' upset win over the Jaguars changes things. It boosts their chances of making the playoffs as a division champion. The way the Giants' defense played, holding the Jaguars without a touchdown for the first three quarters, gives hope of a strong finish to the year after a first half of the season that lacked a quality win. The offense is still not great, ranking 22nd in DVOA. But J.J. McCarthy makes a few plays each game that also provide some optimism, Malik Nabers is one of the NFL's best receivers, Isaiah Likely is having a breakout season and Cam Skattebo generally provides at least a reasonable run game.

The Giants likely aren't going to challenge the 49ers or whoever wins the NFC North for a Super Bowl spot. But their start to the season has more weight behind it after beating a good team.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 11:

1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1, Last week: 2)

The 49ers have faced the No. 1 defense in DVOA (Seattle) and the No. 1 defense in EPA allowed per play (Minnesota). They scored 32 points against the Seahawks and 35 against the Vikings. They got a defensive touchdown in each game but it seems like no defense can hold down the 49ers this season.

While the offense has been fantastic, the 49ers wouldn't be the best team in football through Week 11 without their defense, which has excelled despite Nick Bosa not having a sack all season (he did have two quarterback hits on Sunday night). The 49ers have given up 17 or fewer points in six of their 10 games. They have given up fewer than 300 yards in six games too. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, who replaced Robert Saleh, is doing an excellent job.

The Bills have given up 37 points in four games since their bye. Of course, they have faced an incredibly fortunate run of backup quarterbacks, including Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Cade Klubnik (who replaced an injured Geno Smith in the second half) and Kyle McCord. Still, they have not given up a touchdown in 43 straight drives, the longest streak during a season since the 2019 Patriots, according to the Bills' site . That makes the Thanksgiving primetime matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs one that will help shape this NFL season. Is the Bills' defensive improvement real or because of facing inept quarterbacks?

The Bills' defense struggled early, allowing at least 29 points in five of Buffalo's first six games. The only team to not reach 29 points was the Chargers, who are currently 1-9. But the Bills felt like they weren't far off.

"When teams were scoring on us, I felt like we were playing good ball," Bills defensive end Greg Rousseau said, via the team's site . "We just had to clean up a couple things here and there. We were playing good ball. We weren't really finishing games at the end of the games."

The Bears haven't trailed in five straight games, and that streak brings back memories of the greatest team in franchise history. The last time the Bears went five games without trailing was 1985, when they went the final three games of the regular season and the first two playoff games without trailing, according to Larry Mayer of ChicagoBears.com . The Bears briefly trailed the Patriots 3-0 in Super Bowl XX before winning 46-10.

While this version of the Bears is much different than the famous 1985 team, their pass rush is starting to emerge since Jeffery Simmons came aboard in a trade. On Sunday, they sacked the Saints' Tyler Shough six times (three times by Simmons) and had 24 pressures, which is the most for the team since 2018, according to Next Gen Stats . The defensive improvement will be tested on Thanksgiving in a massive NFC North game against the Lions.

Very good teams are allowed to lose games, even ones in which they're favored. But the teams now ahead of them in the rankings haven't taken many losses, and now the Jaguars have three after a miserable performance in a defeat to the Giants on Sunday . Their chances to get the No. 1 seed in the AFC dropped to 1.6% after Sunday, according to DVOA .

The Jaguars can rightfully complain that a questionable call cost Parker Washington a touchdown . But the offensive issues for the first three quarters are what ultimately cost them the game. The Jaguars, whose offense had been very good before Sunday, had just one drive longer than 23 yards in the first three quarters and didn't score a touchdown. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen took responsibility, saying his plan "maybe had too many things in, moving parts."

"That's a direct reflection of me, and making sure that these guys are prepared well enough," Coen said, via the team's site . "We had been prepared in the majority of our football games, I felt like, and that did not show tonight, especially early on. I put that directly on me."

The Chiefs scored on all five of their first-half drives against the Cardinals, quickly putting away a poor and injured team. One of the stars of the game was tight end Travis Kelce, who is having a remarkable season at age 37. He has 586 yards and four touchdowns, two of which came Sunday against Arizona . His 58.6 yards per game is his most since 2023. There were only three instances of a tight end having more than 400 yards at age 37, and Kelce is already second on that list behind Tony Gonzalez and his 859 yards in 2013. Kelce is on pace for 996 yards.

There were conversations that Kelce could retire after each of the past two seasons, but he's still one of the most productive tight ends in the game. That helps a Chiefs offense that is fourth in EPA per play.

It was a typical Broncos win and not the blowout the 38-24 score indicates. They were outgained 370-351 by the Raiders. Las Vegas rallied to tie the game at 17 after falling behind 17-0 and had the ball at the two-minute warning, down seven points. A pick-6 by Ja'Quan McMillian put the game away in the Broncos' favor.

The best part of the win for the Broncos was perhaps finding an offensive identity. Rookie Jonah Coleman has taken over the backfield, and he had 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 rushing attempts Sunday.

"It's not easy, but he's responded really well to his situation," quarterback Bo Nix said, according to the team's transcripts. "He's been given a great opportunity with RJ Harvey getting hurt (knee) and having a few weeks off. ... It was an impressive performance getting that many carries, running the ball hard."

The Bengals have leaned into being a one-dimensional offense, and it hurt them Monday in a road loss to the Commanders . Washington got consistent pressure on Joe Burrow, including on some well-timed blitzes, and that was partly because it didn't have to worry about Cincinnati's running game. The Bengals rushed 14 times for 31 yards and threw it 40 times. When the Bengals got into field-goal range in the final two minutes, they couldn't run for a first down to grind out the remainder of the clock. They passed on second and third downs and couldn't pick it up. That allowed the Commanders 46 seconds, which they used to drive for a game-winning field goal.

The Bengals should lean on Burrow, who is still tracking to win an MVP after 300 yards and two touchdowns on Monday night. But the lack of a running game, and even the lack of any attempt to try it, could be a big problem for the Bengals in the playoffs.

Detroit's first defensive test without Aidan Hutchinson went well. The Lions allowed just 274 yards and 21 points, and Tampa Bay got 65 yards and a touchdown on a meaningless drive at the end of a game when Detroit led by 17 points. The Lions had four sacks, which was a good sign. The Lions' defense has been much better since the first few weeks of the season, and Sunday's game was without Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell.

The test Thursday will be tougher, with the Chicago Bears coming in with first place in the NFC North on the line. But if Detroit's defense can maintain this level, the Lions might be a Super Bowl contender. That could reveal itself on Thanksgiving.

"Our guys are competitive, man, and they don't want to be counted out," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said of the defense's performance Sunday, via the team's site . "And nobody cares. There are no excuses. And the only way to gain respect is just go about your business, man, and make plays and play together and prove your worth, man."

What we learned about the Vikings on Sunday night, mostly, was that the 49ers are on a much different tier . That's OK, because the 49ers are on a higher tier than all but a few teams.

The blitz was impervious to the 49ers' offense. Minnesota blitzed on 88.9% of San Francisco's dropbacks, and Brock Purdy was 19-of-23 passing for 231 yards and two touchdowns on those plays, according to Pro Football Focus .

"It's one of those things where I told our team, you know, when you play a good team like that and you don't play your best, you're going to get beat," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said, according to the team's site .

That hadn't happened before to the Vikings' defense and is unlikely to repeat, but now Minnesota has to adjust after its worst defensive day of the season.

The NFC West race is probably over, with the 49ers leading it by three games, but Seattle has a shot to make it interesting. The Seahawks play at the 49ers in Week 12 and there's an opportunity to at least make the race interesting.

The big story will be Sam Darnold, whether he can return from injury and how well he plays. The Seahawks are not entertaining the idea of replacing him with Drew Lock. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald defended Darnold, pointing out that he has been injured for most of the season, starting with the first game.

"The beginning of the year for Sam has been a tough road," Macdonald said on Seattle Sports 710, via the team's site . "I can't wait for him to be fully healthy, probably for the first time — minimal times it's happened this year — and get a full week's worth of work and we'll rock and roll from there."

The dream of getting Puka Nacua back for a playoff run is dead, after Nacua had knee surgery that will keep him out the rest of the season . Davante Adams should return but the Rams' offense won't be what was expected before the season, when expectations were sky high.

Even making the playoffs will be difficult because of the Rams' challenging upcoming schedule. Their playoff odds are down to 38.1%, according to DVOA . The Rams practically need a win Wednesday over the Packers, who are one of their main competitors in a very tough NFC wild-card race.

Micah Parsons is set to return for the Packers after practicing in pads Sunday. It's major news for Green Bay to add one of the NFL's best players to the lineup. The Packers were 9-3-1 and leading in the second half at Denver when Parsons tore his ACL last season.

Wednesday at the Rams is a massive game for the Packers and their playoff hopes, and there will be the temptation to play Parsons more than he's ready for in his return. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur is aware of that issue.

"I never wanna place limitations on anybody, but he hasn't played football in a long time," LaFleur said, via Athlon Sports . "So, I think you've got to be conscious of that, and there's probably going to be plays that don't look like him, and there's going to be some plays that do."

Perhaps the biggest development for the Giants on Sunday was defensive end Abdul Carter picking up two sacks. Production had been surprisingly thin for the third overall pick of the 2025 NFL Draft. He had just six sacks in 26 games before Sunday, though his underlying metrics said that sacks were bound to come. Carter also had five quarterback hits.

Carter came in as an elite prospect and if he can start translating his pass rush success into sacks, that could be huge for the Giants. That happened Sunday as the defense played very well against a good Jaguars offense.

"As a defense, we showed what we really about," Carter told CBS after the game . "And for me, I'm the best in the world."

Seeing the Raiders' upset bid fall short was good news for the Browns. Their game against Las Vegas in Week 12, which got flexed to Sunday night, would have been much more interesting in the wild-card race had the Raiders been 5-6 instead of 4-7. It also wasn't bad for Cleveland to see the Steelers slip back to 6-4 with a bad loss at Philadelphia .

The Browns aren't a lock to make the playoffs but the path is very clear. They have two games left against the Bengals and one against the Giants, but the other four are against teams with losing records.

The biggest game in the NFC South this season comes in Tampa Bay next Monday night. The Panthers face the Buccaneers. Tampa Bay gets the season sweep and the tiebreaker with the win. The Falcons and Saints aren't completely out of the running, but Carolina and Tampa Bay look like the two best teams in a bad division.

An old problem popped up again, and it was the run defense. Baltimore had 157 rushing yards, averaging 7.1 yards per attempt. That's a bad weakness to have against the Buccaneers, who lead the NFL at 5 yards per carry.

"They had way too many yards today. Takeaways and stuff is cool, but we got to stop them in the run game," linebacker Tyrel Dodson told the team's site .

The Steelers were showing improvement but the last two weeks are alarming. They were destroyed by the Bengals, then didn't threaten an Eagles team that had lost seven in a row and was on its third quarterback this season. The lingering problem from the game is receiver DK Metcalf getting ejected after another unproductive game. The NFL reportedly won't suspend him , but that doesn't mean Pittsburgh can rely on a player who hasn't done much on the field and whose behavior is unreliable too.

There are also injury concerns at a key spot. Edge rusher Nick Herbig was inactive Sunday because of rib and hip injuries, then Alex Highsmith left the game against the Eagles early because of an ankle injury. The Steelers get the 8-2 Broncos on Friday and the Texans and Jaguars after that. Pittsburgh was once 6-2. It's possible it will be under .500 by mid-December.

David Montgomery could finally make a big impact for the Texans. In his return from injury, he rushed for 107 yards on 26 carries against the Colts. Indianapolis isn't a good team but it was still nice to see something positive from Houston's running game, even if it was in a blowout.

The Texans have been looking for consistency all season, but it's not too late for them to rally for a wild-card spot in a weak race. Their Week 13 game at the Steelers will be a big one for the Texans' playoff hopes. For now, Houston hopes a dominant win over Indianapolis is the start of a streak.

"It's huge," quarterback C.J. Stroud said, according to the team's site . "I think this is a start to something that we need to go on a run with."

18. Washington Commanders (4-5-1, LW: 20)

Jayden Daniels is still capable of looking like a superstar at quarterback. When the Commanders looked like they had lost to the Bengals on a field goal with 46 seconds left, Daniels hit two passes to rookie Antonio Williams for a total of 64 yards, which set up a game-winning field goal as time expired. They were two great throws from Daniels and a great job by Williams to get open. Daniels finished with 289 yards, 122 of which went to Williams.

The Commanders remain two games behind the Giants in the NFC East. But Daniels and Williams kept the Commanders' season alive with two great plays in the final minute on Monday night.

Baker Mayfield's injuries have played a big part in his quiet season, but the Buccaneers still need more from the passing game. Mayfield's top game this season is 243 yards. He had 187 yards against a vulnerable Lions defense on Sunday. Mayfield has just five passing touchdowns in 175 attempts. His yards per attempt of 6.3 is the lowest of his career.

Mayfield was playing through a foot injury Sunday. The Buccaneers need more out of the passing game because they can't keep dropping games and stay in the NFC South race. A loss Monday night to the Panthers might ruin their playoff hopes.

"We're out of mulligans," Mayfield said, according to the team's site.

It's weird to say after giving up 30 points at home to the Titans, but the Cowboys' defense looked better after Mike Pettine took over play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Almost all of the Titans' yards came when they were down double digits and trying to get back in the game. The Titans didn't score a touchdown in the first half.

"Very proud of those guys," Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said of the defense, according to the team's site . "I think the first half was outstanding, but I thought they did a great job of blocking out the noise and working. I was really excited for how they performed."

Fernando Mendoza played well, although his pick-6 in the fourth quarter with the game on the line was a rookie moment. Against a very good Broncos defense, Mendoza had 267 passing yards and three touchdowns. He also rushed for 22 yards. He played well despite being without superstar tight end Brock Bowers, who was out with an ankle injury. For a second NFL start, it was promising.

"He's a first-round pick, first overall for a reason," Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton said, via the team's transcripts. "He's going to be a good player."

The pick-6 just after the two-minute warning ended the Raiders' comeback hopes. There was still progress from Mendoza.

"I felt a lot more comfortable this week than last week," Mendoza said, via the team's site . "They're both great defenses, both top in the league. However, I just felt like I was able to settle in and was able to see the entire field better. I was able to see the entire football field."

Daniel Jones could remain an option for the Patriots after he was suddenly released by the Colts , though head coach Mike Vrabel wouldn't address that Monday. He said Tommy DeVito will start in Week 12.

"We're excited about that, good preseason, and Tommy's improved," Vrabel said .

DeVito struggled when he was forced into action against the Lions in Germany before the bye week. He gets to face the Chargers this weekend, which gives DeVito a chance to impress and keep the job. But it also wouldn't be surprising if Jones finishes the season for a Patriots team that is still in the playoff race.

Years from now, people will look back on the 2026 Ravens, see that Lamar Jackson missed most of the season and attribute Baltimore's poor record to that. And it won't be completely accurate. The defense, which is head coach Jesse Minter's specialty, has been miserable.

Over the Ravens' last five games they have allowed 35, 36, 33, 23 and 35 points. Baltimore lost all five of those games, and its losing streak is at six. Minter took the blame for the Panthers putting together a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, saying "It was just a poor job by me, and that's what it was." Players disagreed.

"I wouldn't necessarily agree with it, truthfully," linebacker Roquan Smith told the team's site . "I thought we were in some really good calls. It comes down to us doing our job. That has been the story all season."

The responsibility for a bad season still falls on Minter, who is in his first season as a head coach. Baltimore is 26th in the NFL in points allowed.

The Saints really don't do anything well. They're 21st in points scored per game and 22nd in yards gained, 23rd in points allowed and 27th in yards allowed. They're 16th in passing yards, 18th in passing yards allowed, 28th in rushing yards and 28th in rushing yards allowed. Even the passing yardage is not that great; Tyler Shough's yards per attempt of 6.2 is better than only four of the 32 qualified quarterbacks this season. Up and down their résumé, nothing stands out as a strength.

It has been a dreadful follow-up to a good second half to last season, which provided false hope for the Saints heading into this season. It looks like a multiple-year rebuild is still in the beginning stages. The good news is the Saints would have the eighth overall pick of the draft if the season ended now .

The problem with the Falcons isn't even their record because they play in the NFC South. But their upcoming schedule is at Vikings, vs. Lions and at Browns. Even one win in those three puts them at 4-9 with four to go. Atlanta will have to play a lot better to stay alive in the playoff hunt over the next three games.

The Falcons had a great two-game stretch against the Packers and Saints and also are the only team to beat the 49ers, so figuring out why they can't play that way most weeks has been tough.

"We got really good players, man," Falcons running back Bijan Robinson said, via the team's site . "Obviously, with the good players, you have to execute at a high level. We have to come together this week and tell ourselves, 'Is this how we want to end the season?'"

Sunday wasn't perfect for the Eagles, with just 214 yards on offense, but their defense is starting to play well. It allowed 255 yards in the 19-16 win over the Steelers, the second straight time the Eagles have held an opponent under 300 yards. Before that stretch, the Eagles hadn't held an opponent to fewer than 300 yards since Week 2, which was the last time Philadelphia had won a game before Sunday.

The Eagles will be tested against a very good Cowboys offense that is coming off a 51-point game against the Titans. But seeing the defense come through, with stellar linebacker play from Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell, gives them hope for a happy Thanksgiving.

The Jets have little to play for, and a loss to the Chargers would have put them in much better draft position next April , but winning is good for any NFL locker room. Even if it's against the Chargers.

"The thing is, a win is a win and that's what we look for and that's the way you play this game," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said, according to the team's site .

There have been some promising developments in the Jets' season, and probably none bigger than the play of edge rusher David Bailey, the second overall pick of the draft. Bailey had two more sacks, giving him 9.5 for the season. Jevon Kearse set the rookie record with 14.5 and Bailey is on pace to break that, though in a 17-game season. He has been undeniably impressive and a big piece for a Jets team that has three first-round picks next year.

Nick Rallis always seemed like an awkward fit as the Cardinals' defensive coordinator, considering he wasn't successful in three previous seasons under an old regime but was retained. First-year head coach Mike LaFleur fired him Monday after another disappointing performance. The Cardinals are 31st in expected points added allowed per play, ahead of only the Cowboys.

The Cardinals haven't been good on defense, but talent certainly seems to be lacking. Safety Budda Baker, the one star the defense has, leads the team with 3.5 sacks. That's a terrible sign. First-round picks up front, like Zaven Collins and Darius Robinson, haven't broken out. We're about to find out if that was because of a coaching problem.

The Colts cutting Daniel Jones less than 24 hours after his 11th straight start to begin the season was odd, even if it ensures they don't have to pay a 2027 injury guarantee. Jones was poor against the Texans, but he was poor all season. He's dead last among NFL starting quarterbacks in EPA per play this season. But the Colts didn't care before Week 11, starting Jones and seemingly never giving any serious consideration to benching him to at least get a look at Anthony Richardson Sr. Cutting a quarterback after starting him all season is a sign of a franchise that isn't making sound decisions.

At least the Colts now can get a look at Richardson, who showed some progress in the preseason. Richardson hasn't shown many signs that he can be an NFL starter, but it's not like the Colts are losing anything by taking another look.

The Dolphins haven't been dominated often. They were dominated Sunday, when they fell behind early and got crushed by a superior Bills team.

One positive point from Sunday was another big game from rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, who had 13 tackles and an interception. He has 93 tackles, a pair of interceptions and a sack this season. Rodriguez was a tremendous college player but he fell to the second round of the NFL Draft. He has already shown that his production at Texas Tech was no fluke and gives the Dolphins one foundational piece in what is going to be a long rebuild.

There wasn't much to be happy with after Sunday's blowout loss. Cam Ward's final line didn't look terrible, but in the first half against a Cowboys defense that is worst in the NFL in many categories, Ward had 55 passing yards and the Titans didn't score a touchdown.

The defense was even worse, giving up 51 points. In Tennessee's last four games it has allowed 491, 510, 459 and 480 yards. The defense was supposed to be much better under head coach Robert Saleh, and it is one of the worst in the NFL. Tennessee has allowed more yards per game than any other team.

"These last couple of weeks, I'm not going to try and sugarcoat anything," Saleh said Monday, according to the team's site . "It's been dog s***."

Good thing the Chargers got that win in Week 10. Losing to the Jets on Sunday at home was a strong indication that Los Angeles might not win again.

At least there were a couple of decent performances on offense. Omarion Hampton continued to get hot late in the season with 89 rushing yards. Justin Herbert had a 119.3 passer rating. His best mark in a game this season before Sunday was 87.5. Unfortunately, Herbert landed in concussion protocol after the loss. Ladd McConkey has had an injury-filled and unproductive season but he had two touchdowns against the Jets. It's not much, especially in a loss. But it's not like there have been many other positives for the Chargers.

articles.title: Watch Jayden Daniels React to Commanders Shocking Bengals & Antonio Williams' Clutch Catch on Video
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders have had a handful of late-game blunders this season, but Jayden Daniels and the offense made sure to avoid another on Monday against the Cincinnati Bengals.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have had a handful of late-game blunders this season, but Jayden Daniels and the offense made sure to avoid another on Monday against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Daniels and wide receiver Antonio Williams helped set up a game-winning field goal after two spectacular plays in the final seconds.

"It's all about trust, and in that moment, I trusted in him to make a play on those back-to-back, and he did," Daniels told ESPN's Laura Rutledge after the win.

"I, personally, live for those moments, high-pressure situations," Daniels said, per The Athletic's David Aldridge . "You want to go out there and make your mark on the game. Obviously, it's not about stats, it's about wins and losses."

The Bengals took a 20-19 lead late in the fourth, giving Daniels and the Commanders just 46 seconds and no timeouts to answer. Washington started its drive on the 28-yard line, but Daniels found Williams for a 22-yard pass on the first play to get the ball to the 50-yard line.

After spiking it to stop the clock, Daniels found Williams to get it into field goal range, but Williams took it all the way down to the eight-yard line, setting up the game-winning field goal from Drew Stevens.

"The same play back-to-back, coach trusts me to make those in those moments," Williams said. "You dream of those on Monday Night Football, so it's a blessing."

While Daniels and Williams played the hero, Washington's defense did a tremendous job against Joe Burrow and the Bengals to keep the Commanders in the game.

"They played a hell of a game," Daniels said. "First half, it took us a minute to get going offensively, and they kept us in the game."

The win helped the Commanders stay in the playoff race after a rough start to the season. Washington still has work to do, but is at least within striking distance of the New York Giants, who lead the NFC East.

"We're just gonna fight. Take it one game at a time, one day at a time," Daniels said. "We just appreciate everyone that stuck with us. We know it wasn't the season that we wanted, how we wanted to start it off, but we still got the second half."

To the winner goes the spoils, and the spoils on Monday was a chance for the Washington Commanders to do some light-hearted trolling of the Cincinnati Bengals and those who picked against the home team.

articles.body:
Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud made a guest appearance on ESPN's ManningCast on Monday night and raved about Washington Commanders rookie linebacker Sonny Styles.

"I'm proud of Sonny, man," Stroud said. "He came in when, I believe, I was in my second year, and he was a safety. He was still a young, skinny kid trying to figure out his way, but man, dude is a baller. I've always known his mindset. He's one of the most mature kids that I've seen coming into Ohio State, and have more a mature mindset, and have a crazy work ethic. ... He's a smart kid."

Stroud was in his third and final year with the Ohio State Buckeyes when Styles arrived as a freshman in 2022. The rookie linebacker played safety for his first two seasons before transitioning to linebacker as a junior in 2024, per Commanders reporter Zach Selby .

Styles compiled five total tackles as the Commanders pulled off a 22-20 upset victory over the Cincinnati Bengals.

articles.title: Joe Burrow Takes Blame, Reacts to Bengals Failing to Beat Commanders amid NFL Super Bowl Push
articles.summary: Going into Monday night's game, anything but a convincing Cincinnati Bengals' victory over the Washington Commanders figured to be a surprising result.
articles.body:
Going into Monday night's game, anything but a convincing Cincinnati Bengals' victory over the Washington Commanders figured to be a surprising result.

The surprise arrived, much to the chagrin of Joe Burrow and the Bengals.

Washington snapped Cincinnati's five-game winning streak with a dramatic 22-20 victory thanks to two long completions from Jayden Daniels to Antonio Williams in the final seconds to set up the game-winning field goal from Drew Stevens.

Daniels After Win: 'I Live for These Moments'

"Obviously, not good enough to win," Burrow told reporters after the game. "We made some plays at the end to put us in a good spot, but it was just not good enough. ... We all can be better, for sure."

It was fitting Stevens played the role of hero, as he went an impressive 5-for-5 on his field-goal attempts in rainy conditions. He also stole the spotlight from his counterpart, as Bengals kicker Evan McPherson drilled a 56-yarder in the final minute to temporarily put the visitors ahead.

Washington's defense also deserves credit, as it held Burrow and the Bengals offense to just 20 points. Considering Cincinnati scored 31 or more points in each of its five games during the winning streak, it was a formidable showing from the Commanders.

Despite the loss, Burrow is certainly still in the middle of the MVP race.

He was excellent again Monday at 28-of-40 for 300 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions, although he will surely want to have the end of his final drive back in hindsight. Cincinnati drove to Washington's 30-yard-line only for the star quarterback to throw a near-interception and take a sack on his final two snaps.

Not only did that sequence make McPherson's field goal much longer, it prevented the Bengals from picking up another first down and running the clock down to make sure their kick was the game's final play.

"If we get the first down, we don't give them a chance to get the ball," Burrow told reporters . "I made a bad play, and the next one they covered pretty well."

Instead, Daniels had a chance to win it in front of the home crowd and delivered thanks to the connection with Williams.

Fortunately for the Bengals, they are still in first place in the AFC North at 7-3 and control their own destiny for a home game in the postseason. However, they are now two games behind the 9-1 Buffalo Bills in the race for the AFC's No. 1 seed and the first-round bye that comes with it.

Considering the 8-2 Kansas City Chiefs, 8-2 Denver Broncos and 7-3 Jacksonville Jaguars are also in that race, this was a costly loss for Burrow and Co.

articles.title: NFL: Washington Commanders beat Joe Burrow's Cincinnati Bengals in upset after last-second field goal from Drew Stevens
articles.summary: Drew Stevens kicks last-second field goal to lift Washington Commanders to surprise win over Joe Burrow's high-flying Cincinnati Bengals; watch an NFL Thanksgiving triple-header live on Sky Sports NFL from 5pm on ThursdaySky Sports
articles.body:
After Evan McPherson put the Bengals ahead 20-19 on a 56-yard field goal, Washington got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts.

Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati eight. The Commanders quarterback spiked it with five seconds left and Stevens did the rest.

Daniels finished with 283 yards passing, Williams had nine catches for 122 yards, and Stevens was five for five on field goals as Washington (4-5-1) remained in the NFC East race, two games behind the division-leading New York Giants.

Burrow threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns for AFC North-leading Cincinnati (7-3), but the Commanders largely held in check a Bengals team that had won five straight, scoring 31 points or more each time.

Washington's defense forced Burrow to settle for checkdowns all night.

The dangerous Bengals receiving duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for just seven catches for 74 yards.

Washington coach Dan Quinn made another questionable late-game decision when he sent Stevens out on fourth-and-one to kick a 41-yard field goal with 2:26 left for a 19-17 lead. That left plenty of time for Burrow, who found Mike Gesicki for a 32-yard completion to move the Bengals into field goal range.

A sack pushed the Bengals back, but McPherson nailed the long kick with 46 seconds remaining.

The game got off to a slow start in rainy conditions but opened up in the second half as the teams traded scores throughout the third quarter.

Burrow's four-yard touchdown pass to Colbie Young put the Bengals ahead 17-10, and the Commanders rallied with three field goals by Stevens.

There was an unexpected stoppage early in the third when the stadium lights went out with the Commanders in the red zone. After a delay that lasted about four minutes, Stevens converted from 36 yards to tie the game at 10-all.

Washington held Cincinnati to three points on its first four drives before Higgins' 31-yard touchdown catch that made it 10-0.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt, activated off injured reserve earlier Monday, scored on a one-yard run for the Commanders with 12 seconds left before halftime.
