articles.title: Se olvidan del mantenimiento… y dejan a oscuras el Commanders - Bengals
articles.standfirst: El partido de la NFL estuvo interrumpido unos cuatro minutos porque el proveedor no había desactivado el mantenimiento programado de la iluminación
articles.summary: El partido de la NFL estuvo interrumpido unos cuatro minutos porque el proveedor no había desactivado el mantenimiento programado de la iluminación
articles.body: El espectáculo del ‘Monday Night Football’ se quedó a oscuras. El encuentro entre Washington Commanders y Cincinnati Bengals tuvo que detenerse durante el tercer cuarto por un apagón en el Northwest Stadium, en Landover, Maryland. La explicación llegó después desde la retransmisión: el mantenimiento de las luces seguía programado pese a que había partido. Washington preparaba una jugada de ataque cuando buena parte de la iluminación se apagó de golpe. Los jugadores tuvieron que esperar y algunos aficionados encendieron las linternas de sus teléfonos mientras se resolvía la incidencia. La interrupción duró aproximadamente cuatro minutos. El comentarista de ESPN Joe Buck explicó posteriormente que el proveedor no había desactivado el mantenimiento habitual de las 22:00, hora local, previsto para los días laborables. "Se olvidaron de que había un partido el lunes por la noche", señaló durante la emisión. Restablecida la iluminación, el partido continuó y acabó con otra escena decisiva, esta vez deportiva: Drew Stevens convirtió un 'field goal' de 26 yardas con el reloj a cero para dar la victoria a Washington por 22-20. Un desenlace que puso fin a la racha de cinco triunfos consecutivos de Cincinnati.

articles.title: Faith, family and lots of football in next six days; Jameson celebrates airborne; Coen says he'd go but didn't
articles.summary: The NFL fills five of the next six days with games, starting with a first-ever Thanksgiving Eve matchup as Micah Parsons returns for the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body: Wednesday evening? There's an NFL game on Thanksgiving eve for the first time ever. Thanksgiving Day? There are NFL games in the afternoon, evening, and at night. Black Friday? There's an NFL game without a discount. Sunday? The NFL is offering 10 games spanning the entire day. NFL'S THANKSGIVING HOLIDAY SCHEDULE THAT FEATURES FIVE GAMES IS DEFINITELY NO TURKEY And, of course, next Monday night? Yes, "Monday Night Football" promises to continue the Joe Buck versus Troy Aikman feud. Once upon a time, Thanksgiving week was about faith and family. And then the NFL decided to become part of the holiday and it was suddenly about faith, family and football. But now the NFL has games scheduled in five of the next six days. So, the same league that snatched Sundays from the church is vying to take away the turkey's starring role on Thanksgiving week. Are you excited? On Wednesday – the NFL is calling it a Thanksgiving Eve matchup – the Green Bay Packers will get star pass rusher Micah Parsons back for the first time this season and will play the Los Angeles Rams, which are trying to live up to all those preseason Super Bowl expectations. RED HOT CHILI PEPPERS DRUMMER CHAD SMITH TO JOIN WU-TANG CLAN FOR LIONS' THANKSGIVING HALFTIME SHOW The NFC North co-leading Detroit Lions and the NFC North co-leading Chicago Bears play in the first game of the day on Thanksgiving Day. "This is good stuff, you know? This is the stuff that gives you the tinglies," Lions coach Dan Campbell said. "Just, you know, big time football, big time opponents, man. "Teeing off on Thanksgiving, we're the first show. It's exciting, man. This is one of the reasons you do it and you love it is for the competition of it and the greatness of all of it, man. Um, So we're looking forward to it." The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles will follow in a game that will match teams trying to convince themselves they're still postseason contenders. Then, in what is perhaps the preview to the AFC Championship game, the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs will play Thanksgiving night – with quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes both coming in with a 5-5 record in 10 career meetings against one another. The Steelers and the Broncos on Friday should be a nice battle now that Steelers receiver DK Metcalf has avoided an NFL suspension and will be able to lose his temper about whatever upsets him next. Welcome to the holiday season, folks. Welcome to the start of the NFL's best time of the year. Dan Campbell manages Jameson Williams sort of Dan Campbell and colorful wide receiver Jameson Williams have this relationship that puts the coach in the role of a mentor, advisor, and something of a school teacher. And Campbell has tried to show patience in bringing his talented player along, but Sunday was a challenge in that department. Williams, known for testing Campbell's limits, caught an electric touchdown pass from Jared Goff and did a front flip into the end zone to celebrate the score. This came after the unfortunate Aidan Hutchinson injury that sent the edge rusher into next season when he blew out a knee while celebrating a sack by going airborne. Last week, Campbell refused to bow to the adversity of losing Hutchinson to a preventable injury by saying he wasn't going to manage his players' celebrations. "I think we all understand what it is, and let’s be smart," Campbell said, "but no, I’m not gonna say, 'Nobody celebrates anymore.' " Williams took that as a green light to do a front flip to celebrate his touchdown on Sunday. That acrobatic move, by the way, fell short of the mark as Williams landed awkwardly. "I tried to land it," Williams told reporters. "I didn't really know what to do, so I just did a front flip. I'm gonna try to land one later in the year for y'all, for sure." And so the testing of Campbell's refusal to manage dangerous celebrations will continue. Hypothetical comes to life for Liam Coen In March of 2025, before he had ever coached a game for the Jacksonville Jaguars, Liam Coen visited with the guys from "Pardon My Take" and was given a hypothetical situation to consider. He was trailing by 8 points, at the 8 yard line, facing a fourth down situation. Does he go for it or kick a field goal? "Gotta go for it," Coen said. "You're going to have to use that [opportunity] when you're down there. When you're down there and you have an opportunity to score a touchdown, you're that close, we all know how hard it is to score in the red zone in this league, so when you're down there you have to use your op. You have to be aggressive there." On Sunday, against the New York Giants, Coen's team was at the New York Giants' 8 yard line on fourth down and trailing by 8 points with 3:43 to play. So, the exact hypothetical situation come to life. Coen kicked the field goal to trail by five points. His offense never saw the ball again. And the Jaguars lost the game. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Niners reward John Lynch The 49ers agreed to a contract extension with John Lynch as their president of football operations and general manager, as Fox Sports first reported and the team confirmed. This is obviously the best outcome for all parties because Lynch's current contract was set to expire after the season and he's done a fabulous job not only loading but reloading talent onto that team when the guys he loads get hurt – as Mike Evans, Christian Kirk and even Deebo Samuel, who was brought in to help when other guys got injured, got injured himself. It doesn't get easier as the team has lost right tackle Colton McKivits to a horrible injury. The 49ers are expected to move Vederian Lowe into the starting spot and that highlights Lynch's signing of Lowe as a swing tackle in the offseason. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Chris Rodriguez Jr. and the Best Week 12 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: With the fantasy football playoffs fast approaching, Week 12 of the 2026 NFL season represents a critical opportunity for managers to strengthen their rosters via the waiver wire.
articles.body:
With the fantasy football playoffs fast approaching, Week 12 of the 2026 NFL season represents a critical opportunity for managers to strengthen their rosters via the waiver wire.

Whether you are cruising to a No. 1 seed, locked into a bitter battle for one of the remaining spots on the postseason bracket or need to go on an undefeated run to even reach the playoffs, it's imperative to have your lineup in the best shape possible before the race gets even tighter come December.

Injuries, a lack of Week 12 byes and other revelations around the league have created several intriguing options to pad out your depth and even nab a potential starter off the free-agent pile.

There are potential upgrades lurking at every position, so be sure to make some moves and get your lineup set for a packed NFL Thanksgiving week schedule that runs from Wednesday through Monday.

Suggestions are available in approximately half or more of all Yahoo! Sports leagues. Fantasy points and rankings are courtesy of FantasyPros ' PPR data. Suggested free-agent acquisition budget (FAAB) bids are based on a $100 starting budget.

Deshaun Watson, Cleveland Browns (14 Percent Rostered)

Deshaun Watson has emerged as a viable streaming option for Week 12 as his Browns prepare to face the Raiders.

Watson's 2026 campaign started slow and has been rocky, but he's thrown for at least 300 yards in three consecutive starts and has added valuable production with his legs. That dual-threat capability gives him a far higher floor than most other quarterbacks available on waivers at this point in the season.

The matchup also works in Watson's favor, as Las Vegas has struggled defensively. The Raiders have given up at least 30 points in seven of their last eight games and are allowing 19.2 points per game to opposing QBs—the fifth-most in the league this year.

Watson may not be the type of quarterback managers can plug-and-play on a weekly basis, but he's a reasonable short-term starter with upside. If you need a streamer to get you through, Watson should be your first choice.

Fernando Mendoza, Las Vegas Raiders (18 Percent Rostered)

Fernando Mendoza is on the cusp of becoming a reliable fantasy option. He looked every bit of an inexperienced rookie during his first start in Week 10, but his performance against the Broncos on Sunday offered a glimpse of his unlimited upside.

The rookie completed 18 of his 37 passes for 267 yards and a whopping three touchdown passes against Denver's stingy defense in Week 11. Although he took five sacks and was responsible for a pick-six, he clearly has the talent to thrive at the NFL level. He'll look to further improve in Week 12 during a clash with the Browns with real potential to turn into a barnburner.

The Browns are a noticeable step down from the two staunch defenses Mendoza was forced to contend with during his first two starts. If he can combine the rushing success (22 yards and a touchdown on six carries) he had against Seattle in Week 10 with the passing aptitude he showed against the Broncos last week, Mendoza could breeze to his first top-10 career fantasy finish.

Anthony Richardson, Indianapolis Colts (1 Percent Rostered)

Anthony Richardson is back on the fantasy radar after the Colts shockingly moved on from Daniel Jones this past week. With the 2023 first-round pick getting a final opportunity to prove himself in Indy, he could be a league-winning pickup for managers willing to roll the dice.

Richardson's passing accuracy has been and remains a significant concern in any of his starts, but unparalleled athleticism and elite rushing ability give him a clear advantage in fantasy.

He's used his legs to rack up some massive fantasy days, including two top-five finishes in his first three career starts and another pair of top-five outings during his shaky sophomore campaign.

Remember that Richardson is more likely to struggle mightily than succeed. Despite the rushing upside, he's stepping into a dreadful situation with a severely undermanned supporting cast that was gutted by the trade deadline and injury.

Consider Richardson a high-risk, high-reward option for truly desperate managers.

Chris Rodriguez Jr., Jacksonville Jaguars (33 Percent Rostered)

Chris Rodriguez Jr. is shaping up to be the smartest waiver-wire addition managers can make in Week 12. While he's not guaranteed to be a slam-dunk plug-and-play starter, he offers a ridiculous amount of value if Bhayshul Tuten isn't able to give it a go for Jacksonville's Week 12 contest against Tennessee.

With Tuten dealing with a nagging ankle injury, Rodriguez has potential to step into a feature role for the Jags. While Rodriguez has primarily worked as Tuten's backup this season, he's been efficient with his limited touches. He's already been on the flex radar in deeper leagues by recording 261 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 63 totes on the year, but a lack of regular carries and limited passing game touches (he has just four receptions for 49 yards in 2026) has kept him from seeing wider usage.

Expect Rodriguez to see a major increase in volume should Tuten miss time. He proved he can handle a large workload during the back half of the 2025 season, a stretch in which he averaged a shade over 12 carries and scored five touchdowns in the seven games he was active for between Weeks 9-18.

With a favorable matchup against Tennessee approaching and Tuten looking like he may need some rest, Rodriguez should be a priority addition for any RB-needy manager.

Justice Hill, Baltimore Ravens (21 Percent Rostered)

Justice Hill has quietly become a reliable fantasy option over the last month. The Ravens running back has tallied 23 targets and converted those into 16 receptions for 88 yards and a score. He's posted a pair of top-10 finishes in that span, including a 17.6-point effort against the Panthers on Sunday.

Despite Derrick Henry taking the lion's share of rushing work, Hill's steady usage in a Lamar Jackson-less passing attack gives him an extremely stable floor. The veteran has also answered the call when his number is called as a rusher, averaging an impressive 8.2 yards per carry over the last four games.

Hill also has strong value as a handcuff to Henry. If the superstar starter ultimately misses time, Hill would be in line for a significant increase in touches. That makes him worth rostering in all formats, so be sure to put a claim in if he's available in your league.

Will Shipley, Philadelphia Eagles (2 Percent Rostered)

Will Shipley became one of the most popular fantasy football waiver wire targets after Saquon Barkley went down with an injury earlier this season, but the hype was short lived after Shipley picked up an injury of his own in his first start of 2026. Shipley was activated in Week 11 and could be in line for a far larger role than the one he played in his first game back.

While Shipley only contributed nine yards on four rushing attempts against the Steelers, he could soon see flex-worthy volume as the primary backup to Barkley. The Eagles are well out of playoff contention and are already looking forward to next season after a 3-7 start, so it wouldn't be a surprise if they exercise caution with Barkley and try to keep him healthy for 2027.

With Philly facing a short turnaround ahead of a Thanksgiving matchup, Barkley could sit due to the arm injury he appeared to suffer late in Week 11's victory over Pittsburgh. Shipley would be the primary beneficiary if Barkley is absent or limited against the Cowboys and their sieve-like defense that has allowed a league-most 23.6 fantasy points per game to opposing backs in 2026.

Consider Shipley a speculative addition rather than a must-start pickup, but his potential workload makes him worth the investment.

Caleb Douglas, Miami Dolphins (46 Percent Rostered)

Caleb Douglas has been flashing his elite potential despite some wild inconsistency plaguing Miami's quarterback position.

While starter Malik Willis has been sidelined for the last two weeks, the rookie has quickly become backup Kyle McCord's favorite target. He's racked up a hefty 18 looks over the past fortnight, and while the production (5/101/0) in those contests was modest, the target volume is encouraging and worth gambling on for fantasy purposes.

Douglas will get a chance to turn his ample opportunities into real production when the 'Phins face a downtrodden Jets defense in Week 12. The 23-year-old already torched this secondary for a pair of touchdowns in Week 7 and could continue to feast in the rematch.

Don't expect Douglas to evolve into an every-week option this season, but he's a good enough spot-starter to get you through inevitable injuries and upcoming bye weeks.

Chimere Dike, Tennessee Titans (13 Percent Rostered)

Chimere Dike has become a relevant fantasy option following Wan'Dale Robinson's season-ending injury. While he rarely saw the field over the first seven weeks of the 2026 campaign (logging just 52 offensive snaps in total during that span), Dike has averaged 57 offensive snaps in each of his last three games.

Dike has turned that increased involvement into 13 receptions for 156 yards and a touchdown on 16 targets in that span. He posted a top-10 finish in Week 8 and had another productive performance against Dallas on Sunday, catching six passes for 69 yards on seven targets to earn a top-25 finish.

The 24-year-old's role will only grow as Tennessee tries to develop its young wideouts while playing out the string. A Week 12 matchup against Jacksonville isn't an ideal fantasy matchup, but Dike's recent target volume still makes him an appealing depth addition and deep-league starter.

Konata Mumpfield, Los Angeles Rams (13 Percent Rostered)

Konata Mumpfield looks in line for a larger opportunity with the Rams dealing with major injuries at wide receiver. Puka Nacua is expected to miss the remainder of the regular season following knee surgery, while Davante Adams is still sidelined with a hamstring injury and isn't likely to return for several more weeks.

Mumpfield took advantage of an expanded workload when Nacua missed time earlier in the year, recording four receptions for 93 yards and a touchdown against Denver in Week 3. That has been the high-water mark for the second-year wideout this season, but his best is likely still to come.

If you can afford the roster spot and need some WR help, Mumpfield is a good lottery ticket to snatch up on waivers.

Evan Engram, Denver Broncos (2 Percent Rostered)

Tight end streaming options remain bleak going into Week 12, but Evan Engram is worth a look following his impressive outing against the Raiders.

Engram has steadily seen his involvement in Denver's passing attack grow, culminating with the longtime veteran reeling in six of eight targets for 74 yards during a Week 11 win over Las Vegas.

He's now recorded 10 receptions on 13 targets over his last two games, suggesting the production could be more than the flash in the pan his TE8 finish in Week 1 ended up being.

While Engram lacks scoring upside, his target volume is valuable at a position where reliable looks are difficult to find on waivers. Consider him a reasonable low-cost option if you need immediate help at tight end.

Tyler Higbee, Los Angeles Rams (22 Percent Rostered)

Tyler Higbee might benefit from the injuries ravaging the Rams' receiving corps and tight ends room more than any other player. Terrance Ferguson, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are all out of action, leaving star signal-caller Matthew Stafford with a dearth of proven receivers.

Higbee has potential to be the next man up and could become a linchpin in the passing game as the team fights for a playoff berth. He began making the most of this expanded workload before the team's Week 11 bye, catching three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown. His 10.7 points were good for a TE8 finish, his best showing since a 20.2-point explosion in Week 3.

Consider Higbee a useful short-term streamer for managers seeking upside at the tight end position.

Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers (37 Percent Rostered)

Pat Freiermuth has been producing at a steady level over the past month and has a favorable matchup in Week 12, making him the safest streaming TE option widely available on waivers.

The Steelers tight end has recorded top-15 finishes in each of his last three games. While he didn't score a touchdown on Sunday like he did the previous two contests, he had his most prolific pass-catching performance since Week 5 by hauling in all five of his targets for 39 yards.

With the Broncos likely to lock up Pittsburgh's receivers in their upcoming showdown, Freiermuth should see five-plus targets and convert those into a useful amount of receptions and yards to move the needle in fantasy.

If he can find the end zone for the sixth time this season, he'll be a shoo-in for a top-eight finish.

articles.title: 5 Trade Landing Spots For Veterans Needing Change of Scenery in 2027 NFL Offseason
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline may have come and gone, but the market will quickly heat up when it reopens at the start of the 2027 offseason.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline may have come and gone, but the market will quickly heat up when it reopens at the start of the 2027 offseason.

Several high-profile names could earn a fresh start with a different team this spring. Regardless of whether they are aging veterans who have fallen out of favor with their current club or once-promising young talents who declined suddenly, a trade could benefit all parties involved.

While blockbuster deals aren't easy to pull off in the NFL, a recent trend of player movement suggests several big names will be moved before next year's campaign kicks off.

With that in mind, here's a look at these five trade landing spots for veterans desperately in need of a change of scenery in the 2027 NFL offseason.

The Los Angeles Chargers' struggles have been one of the biggest storylines of the 2026 NFL season.

The myriad issues the club has contended with could lead to a complete overhaul during the upcoming offseason, changes that could even result in a once-inconceivable Justin Herbert trade taking place.

With Herbert looking utterly broken over the first 10 games of the season, the Bolts could give serious consideration to moving on from the two-time Pro Bowler and 2020 Offensive Rookie of the Year. He is completing a career-worst 62.4 percent of his throws, has more interceptions (11) than touchdown passes (8) and has won just one of his 10 starts.

Despite the fall from grace, the signal-caller could still command a king's ransom in a trade. Leading up to this year's deadline, an unnamed front-office executive told SI.com's Gilberto Manzano that a Herbert trade would need to include at least three first-round picks, along with lower-round selections and/or established players.

While it's an exorbitant cost to pay for any passer—let alone one in the midst of the type of season Herbert is currently mired in—the New York Jets might just be willing to give up that sort of package to address their longstanding quarterback woes.

Gang Green has been stockpiling picks and will eventually look to cash those chips in. If the draft began today, the team would select at Nos. 4, 5 and 15 overall in addition to No. 36 in Round 2 and No. 70 in Round 3. There's clearly enough capital here to get a deal done if New York's brass decides to make a run at Herbert.

While they could use one of these selections to simply draft a signal-caller, that strategy hasn't worked out well for the organization. The Jets have taken two swings on the position in the last decade, whiffing on both Zach Wilson (No. 2 overall in 2021) and Sam Darnold (No. 3 in 2018). The Jets haven't picked a quarterback who led them to a Super Bowl title since selecting Joe Namath in the first round of the 1965 AFL draft.

This would be the ultimate high-risk, high-reward trade. If Gang Green truly believes Herbert could follow in Namath's footsteps and lead them to a Super Bowl, the heavy costs of acquiring the quarterback would be well worth it. If Herbert can't rekindle the elite form he displayed earlier in his career, it would doom New York to another decade of mediocrity.

Despite multiple attempts to address the position in recent seasons, the Kansas City Chiefs still need a legitimate star wide receiver to pair with Patrick Mahomes. DK Metcalf has real potential to be the answer to this glaring problem.

Metcalf could be available given how he's disappointed within a tepid Aaron Rodgers-led Pittsburgh Steelers offense. He mustered a career-worst 850 receiving yards last year and is on an even worse pace in 2026.

Metcalf has only recorded 36 receptions for 434 yards and two touchdowns on the year, putting him well off the 73-reception, 1,054-receiving yard, eight-touchdown pace he averaged during his time with the Seattle Seahawks. A change of scenery could be exactly what he needs to rejuvenate his career.

The 28-year-old remains an imposing physical presence at 6'4", 235 pounds and possesses the speed and athleticism to give opposing defenses fits. Those traits would be particularly valuable to Kansas City's offense, which has struggled to consistently generate explosive plays from the receiving corps following the departure of Tyreek Hill in 2022.

The Steelers may not want to give up on a player they surrendered a second-round pick to acquire ahead of the 2025 campaign and signed to a four-year, $132 million extension, but the time could be right to move on.

Pittsburgh may find the best path forward will be stripping the roster down to the studs if Rodgers isn't able to get the job done in what is expected to be his final NFL season. Metcalf is under contract through the 2029 season, but could be one of the first dominos to fall if the team opts to enter a full rebuilding phase this offseason.

The Chiefs shouldn't hesitate to capitalize if the Steelers host a fire sale, picking up Metcalf and giving him a chance to prove he's still elite by working alongside Mahomes.

The Buffalo Bills have looked like a legitimate Super Bowl contender during their NFL-best 9-1 start to the 2026 season, but a shaky pass defense could be their Achilles' heel.

If Buffalo comes up short in the playoffs yet again, general manager Brandon Beane will have to make a splash on the trade market to fix things.

Cooper DeJean should be atop Beane's wish list, as the Philadelphia Eagles cornerback has potential to be an impact talent in Buffalo's secondary. He also happens to be in need of a change of scenery after suffering a severe regression in Year 3 of his NFL career.

While DeJean began his career red-hot—playing a key role for the Eagles during their Super Bowl run as a rookie in 2024 before earning an All-Pro nod as a sophomore the next season—he's fallen off significantly in 2026. After giving up just one TD over his first 32 regular-season games combined, he has allowed four touchdowns in coverage over the first 10 contests of this season.

Buffalo would provide DeJean an opportunity to reset his career while addressing arguably the most significant weakness on the roster. The Bills have surrendered 226.3 passing yards per game and 15 total passing touchdowns through 10 contests while constantly shuffling the deck in the secondary to try to find a modicum of stability.

At just 23 years of age, DeJean still has plenty of upside to offer and may not have even reached his ceiling yet. Although it would be painful to move on from him, the Eagles would benefit far more from acquiring several draft picks to reshape the roster with than the current version of DeJean.

NFL Teams That Could Trade Up for Jeremiah Smith 📈

The Cleveland Browns were willing to trade away a generational edge-rusher in Myles Garrett largely due to the fact that they landed one of the league's most promising young defensive ends in Jared Verse as part of the blockbuster deal.

Unfortunately, Verse hasn't come close to filling the massive void Garrett left behind.

Verse is struggling immensely in Cleveland, recording a mere 20 tackles and zero sacks over his first 10 games with the organization. He's created just seven pressures and has failed to disrupt in the backfield with any sort of consistency.

The 2024 Defensive Rookie of the Year and two-time Pro Bowler recently acknowledged that a " mental block " has negatively impacted his performances. Verse has begun working with the team's psychiatrist to overcome his struggles and return to his previous level of play.

If he can't find a way to right the ship in the back half of the campaign, it may make more sense for the Browns to try and deal him while he still has value and upside.

Sending Verse back to the Los Angeles Rams makes sense for both organizations. The Rams have a talent-laden defensive front with Garrett and Aaron Donald leading the way, but bringing back the youthful Verse would give them a player to build their defense around for the long haul.

The Rams also know how to get the most out of Verse within their system. After selecting him on Day 1 of the 2024 draft, he went on to earn Defensive Rookie of the Year honors and back-to-back Pro Bowl nods.

Verse tallied 124 tackles and 12 sacks over those two seasons and could get back to playing that same high level of football if he returns to Los Angeles in 2027.

Rumors swirled that the Jacksonville Jaguars might trade Brian Thomas Jr. at the 2026 deadline, but the team ultimately stood pat and held onto the struggling wideout.

Barring a massive turnaround over the next two months, the Jags won't have much reason to hesitate if a team proposes a deal for Thomas during the 2027 offseason.

While general manager James Gladstone said after the deadline that "We have a ton of value when it comes to BTJ. His role and what I imagine his contribution is going to be [is] notable", that value hasn't materialized in any tangible way. Although he scored a touchdown on Sunday, Thomas has notched a meager four catches for 47 yards on seven targets across the two games Jacksonville has played since the deadline.

Thomas could still save his career, but it's likely going to take a trade to do so.

The wideout burst onto the scene with an eye-popping 87/1,282/10 receiving line as a first-round rookie in 2024, but has massively regressed since head coach Liam Coen took the reins in 2025.

With Thomas only catching 48 balls for 707 receiving yards and two touchdowns last year and recording a dreadful 14/167/3 receiving line in 10 games this year, it's clear that he's not a fit for this system.

The San Francisco 49ers would be an intriguing trade partner, with head coach Kyle Shanahan having a proven track record of rehabilitating veteran castoffs. They also desperately need wide receivers who can stay healthy, one of the few things Thomas has consistently done throughout his career—missing just three contests since entering the league.

Although San Francisco is off to a sizzling 9-1 start, the receiving corps has been a revolving door due to injury. Getting some stability would be a huge boon to the offense, especially if the 24-year-old Thomas returns to Pro Bowl form and emerges as the club's WR1 for the foreseeable future.

articles.title: Week 12 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Lineup Advice and Smart Sleepers to Exploit
articles.summary: It's Thanksgiving Week, which means a couple of different things for fantasy footballers. Firstly, we're about to have games on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday, and Monday in Week 12.
articles.body:
It's Thanksgiving Week, which means a couple of different things for fantasy footballers. Firstly, we're about to have games on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday, and Monday in Week 12.

Secondly, all 32 teams will be in action, so the bye-week blues won't be a factor this week.

Injuries and difficult matchups will still leave managers with some difficult decisions, however. Here, you'll find some early start/sit advice and potential sleepers to consider in Week 12. All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Start: Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars

Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars had a rough go of it against the New York Giants on Sunday. Typically a reliable fantasy starter, Lawrence tossed a pair of interceptions and finished with a modest 14.7 fantasy points.

However, Lawrence should rebound in Week 12, as the Jags will host the rival Tennessee Titans. Tennessee's defense was a sieve against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 11, and no team has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season than the Titans.

The Minnesota Vikings defense struggled mightily against Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday night. However, that's no reason to trust Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. in Week 12.

Penix has been inconsistent all season, and he hasn't shown the poise needed to consistently beat Minnesota's blitz-heavy defense. The Vikings have surrendered the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing QBs on the season, and they should return to form against Atlanta.

Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy fared about as well as Lawrence in Week 11, finishing with just 14.2 fantasy points. However, he could be a very strong play against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 12.

Indianapolis has surrendered the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing QBs this season, and its defense looked absolutely lifeless last Thursday. McCarthy is still rostered in only 23 percent of fantasy leagues.

Start: Kenny Gainwell, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Kenny Gainwell is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' No. 2 back behind Bucky Irving, and both backs were stymied by the Detroit Lions on the ground on Sunday. However, Gainwell caught four passes and finished with a respectable 9.9 fantasy points anyway.

He should have a much better stat line this week, as the Bucs will host the rival Carolina Panthers. No team has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing RBs this season than Carolina.

Sit: MarShawn Lloyd, RB, Green Bay Packers

Even with Josh Jacobs (finger) unlikely to play on Wednesday, managers should avoid Green Bay Packers running back MarShawn Lloyd against the Los Angeles Rams. Lloyd caught three passes in Green Bay's last game but only logged four carries, as Kaleb Johnson took over as the leading rusher.

The Rams, meanwhile, have surrendered the fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs this season.

Sleeper: Chris Rodriguez Jr., Jacksonville Jaguars

Bhayshul Tuten has been battling foot and ankle injuries, and he limped off the field late in Sunday's contest. He also averaged just 3.3 yards per carry against the Giants, while Chris Rodriguez Jr. averaged seven yards per carry—albeit on four attempts.

Rodriguez has some legitimate sleeper value this week against a Titans defense that has surrendered more than 22 fantasy points to opposing backfields weekly. He's rostered in only 29 percent of fantasy leagues.

In Jacoby Brissett's first start for the Baltimore Ravens, the offense struggled to funnel the football to top receiver Zay Flowers. That was far less of an issue in Week 11, as Flowers finished with eight catches and 97 yards—though he did lose 13 yards on a failed sweep.

Now that Brissett has established some chemistry with Flowers, the receiver is back to being a weekly must-start. He has a good matchup this week against the Houston Texans, who have surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing WRs.

The 49ers' offense was terrific against the Vikings, thanks in large part to the return of Mike Evans. However, the return of Evans and the recent addition of Keenan Allen have hurt Deebo Samuel's fantasy value.

Samuel had three catches and two carries for 47 yards against Minnesota. This week, he'll face a Seattle Seahawks defense that has surrendered the fewest fantasy points to opposing WRs.

Sleeper: Konata Mumpfield, Los Angeles Rams

Puka Nacua recently underwent knee surgery and is expected to miss the rest of the season. The Rams aren't getting Davante Adams (hamstring) back in the near future either. That gives Konata Mumpfield a ton of upside in all formats moving forward.

Mumpfield yielded 11.1 fantasy points in his last outing, and he's still only rostered in 19 percent of fantasy leagues. He'll face a middle-of-the-road Packers defense on Wednesday.

Start: Pat Freiermuth, Pittsburgh Steelers

The Pittsburgh Steelers' offense stunk it up against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, and it's impossible to trust Pittsburgh against the Denver Broncos in Friday's game. However, it is reasonable to trust tight end Pat Freiermuth.

Freiermuth caught five passes against Philly, and he could be Aaron Rodgers' go-to target against Denver. The Broncos have surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends in 2026.

It's not really reasonable to trust anything about the Los Angeles Chargers at this point. That includes tight end David Njoku, who was a regular fantasy producer with the Cleveland Browns when healthy.

Njoku has caught just two of four targets in two games since his return from injured reserve. This week, he'll face a New England Patriots defense that has surrendered the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing TEs.

Njoku is probably available on the free-agent pile in most leagues and can stay there. Rams tight end Tyler Higbee should be scooped up ASAP. He's likely to be a high-volume target with Nacua and Adams both sidelined, and he's only rostered in 19 percent of leagues.

Higbee tallied 10.7 fantasy points in his last outing. He should have a high PPR floor this week, even against a Packers defense that has been fairly stout against opposing TEs.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Clock Controversy in Bengals' Loss to Commanders Explained by NFL Rules Analyst in New Video
articles.summary: While the operator erred in running down the clock, the officiating crew correctly handled the end of Monday's 22-20 win for the Washington Commanders over the Cincinnati Bengals.
articles.body:
While the operator erred in running down the clock, the officiating crew correctly handled the end of Monday's 22-20 win for the Washington Commanders over the Cincinnati Bengals.

Russell Yurk, the rules analyst for Monday Night Football , said the Bengals should've had two seconds after Drew Stevens connected on his 26-yard field goal. However, the referees were prohibited from adding time back to the clock in that situation:

Daniels After Win: 'I Live for These Moments'

It's not exactly a satisfactory outcome when someone acknowledges a mistake was made but says nothing could be done to rectify it. The Bengals have a reason to feel a little slighted.

But the result likely would've been the same if Cincinnati had fielded the ensuing kickoff. The return needed to go for a touchdown, or a fair catch could've set up one last prayer.

The Bengals didn't start or finish well. They were scoreless in the first quarter and let Washington control the ball for the majority of the fourth.

"Tough to find a rhythm early. Those first couple drives, obviously we weren't at our best," coach Zac Taylor said . "They did a great job, they were aggressive. They took the fight to us a little bit. After that, I thought we found a really good rhythm the last two drives of the first half and coming out in the second half. We just weren't able to finish there at the end of the game. Those last two drives are what got us."

The defense also allowed its second-most yards (428) of the season. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels went 23-of-35 for 289 yards through the air and ran for 55 yards.

Stevens' field goal was the decisive blow, but Cincinnati lost this game before his kick sailed through the uprights.

articles.title: Drew Stevens Drops Must-See Quote in Viral Video After Game-Winning Kick for Commanders vs. Bengals
articles.summary: Washington Commanders kicker Drew Stevens wanted to create a memorable moment for his future children.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders kicker Drew Stevens wanted to create a memorable moment for his future children.

After lifting the Commanders to a 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday Night Football with a last-second 26-yard field goal, Stevens revealed his epic internal monologue that helped him rise to the occasion.

"Authentic Drew Stevens. You really want to know what I tell myself?" Stevens asked reporters. "I sit there, and I'm like, 'OK, I'm gonna have kids. Am I gonna tell my kids that their dad was a little... you know. Am I gonna tell my kids that? Or am I gonna tell my kids that, yeah, your dad walked out there and he drilled it, and he was ready for it?' That's what I'm gonna tell them, because that's how it happened."

Daniels After Win: 'I Live for These Moments'

The Commanders appeared to be on their way to a loss in front of their home fans at Northwest Stadium when Bengals kicker Evan McPherson made a 56-yard field goal with 0:46 left in regulation to give his team a 20-19 lead. However, Washington star quarterback Jayden Daniels led a nail-biting five-play drive to set up Stevens' game-winner.

The Commanders improved to 4-5-1 and are still very much alive in the wide-open NFC East.

Washington will try to earn its third straight win when it meets the Arizona Cardinals (3-8) on Sunday.

articles.title: New NFL MVP Odds Updated as Joe Burrow Loses After Brock Purdy's Impressive Box Score Stats in Win
articles.summary: With Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season in the books, San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is a slight MVP favorite over the Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow.
articles.body:
With Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season in the books, San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is a slight MVP favorite over the Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow.

Purdy (+110) and Burrow (+140) are neck and neck at FanDuel Sportsbook . Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen are next on the list and have some ground to make up at +1000.

Purdy was one of the week's standout performers as he efficiently sliced through the Minnesota Vikings secondary in a 35-10 win. And with the Niners improving to 9-1, it's no surprise to see him vault to the top in the MVP race.

Burrow is leading the NFL in passing yards (3,095) and touchdown passes (29), and the Bengals still have a one-game lead on the Cleveland Browns for first place in the AFC North.

The three-time Pro Bowler will be difficult to beat for MVP if he stays this prolific while guiding Cincinnati to the postseason.

Purdy's efficiency is setting him apart rather than sheer volume. He's first in quarterback rating (118.2) and QBR (84.6), and his 9.0 yards per attempt are the highest of any qualified passer.

The Vikings own one of the best pass defenses, yet they had no answer for Purdy. San Francisco scored touchdowns on three of its first four drives.

"Best player in the game right now," Niners receiver Mike Evans told reporters of his QB. "He's super dialed in. The way he prepares, the way he competes, he's tough. I always thought he's been underrated."

If the season ended right now, Burrow and Purdy would both have credible MVP claims. One can only hope this carries on for the rest of the year, and Mahomes could make it a three-way battle given how he and the Chiefs are performing right now.

articles.title: Michael Irvin Talks Cowboys, Super Bowl, Packers vs. Rams and Miami QB Mensah in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys legend Michael Irvin thinks his former team will be able to keep their star wide receiving duo of George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb together past the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys legend Michael Irvin thinks his former team will be able to keep their star wide receiving duo of George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb together past the 2026 season.

Pickens is playing on a one-year franchise tag after the Cowboys decided against negotiating a long-term extension last spring.

"I know George's dad. He talks about how much George Pickens loves it here. It's where he wants to be," Irvin told Bleacher Report. "So, I'm going to go by what I hear... I think they get it here, and I think he gets it here, and he wants to be here, and hopefully that works out."

Pickens followed up a Week 10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in which he recorded a season-high 145 receiving yards and three touchdown catches with 102 yards and a touchdown last Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Lamb added 132 yards and another score in the 51-30 win.

Irvin compared that duo to himself and Alvin Harper, with whom he won two of his three Super Bowls with the Cowboys, when bringing up Pickens and Lamb sitting out the start of a November 2025 game against the Las Vegas Raiders after missing curfew together.

"All I care about is, when they miss curfew, they were together," Irvin said. "You've got something there, 'cause me and Alvin Harper, we've done it together... I know how close those two guys are, and that's why I say, hopefully, it'll work out."

Irvin expressed less confidence in Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who has led Dallas to a 5-6 start ahead of the team's upcoming Thanksgiving matchup against the visiting Philadelphia Eagles.

The Cowboys have ranked fifth in the NFL in points scored per drive so far this season, but that offense has been too inconsistent to cover for one of the least effective defenses in the NFL.

"I wish I could take it like a great brain surgeon, cutting out the good parts that we can use and pulling away the bad parts," Irvin said. "Coach Schottenheimer is part of the good parts. He's part of that 40-point offense... but he's also part of that defense and the hiring process."

Before Irvin watches Schottenheimer try to campaign for his long-term job security with a holiday win, the former Cowboys star will be in the Netflix broadcast booth when the Green Bay Packers play the Los Angeles Rams on Thanksgiving Eve Wednesday night.

Although Irvin doesn't see either of these teams as Super Bowl finalists— his picks ahead of Week 11 were for the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills to make the AFC title game as the San Francisco 49ers and Chicago Bears battle for NFC championship— Wednesday's outcome could have a significant impact on the NFC playoff picture.

"In the NFL, we say after Thanksgiving, that's when the real stuff starts," Irvin said. "This pre-Thanksgiving game is the real stuff. It's like a pre-Thanksgiving, but a pre-playoff game for those teams also."

Irvin feels Packers coach Matt LaFleur will need to get more creative with his passing game to slow the momentum of the Rams. Matthew Stafford has led his team to four straight wins despite losing Davante Adams and Puka Nacua to injuries, while Jordan Love and the Packers are coming off a blowout loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

"They're trying to stick to what they do, and they like to go up the field and throw passes up the field, and the Vikings aren't giving you that time," Irvin said about the Packers' struggles in Week 10. "So it's like, you've got to throw quick pass game here. And a few times, they did it, it worked, but they got away from it.

"They want to always throw the big passes. You've got to run the ball and get rid of the ball quickly. The Rams don't do that as well as the Vikings, but I'm sure the Rams will be doing some of that until you show them that you can stop it."

Irvin said he would "love" for Los Angeles to host more Thanksgiving Eve games in the future, in part so that players can have a warm-weather destination before holiday games take place in colder cities like Detroit.

Irvin has plenty of experience with holiday matchups. He competed in 10 Thanksgiving games with the Cowboys, for which he set a franchise record with six holiday touchdown catches.

The most memorable game from that slate arguably featured Irvin catching a touchdown pass from Troy Aikman in a 1995 win over the Kansas City Chiefs, but Irvin says the game he thinks of every Thanksgiving is a 1993 loss to the Miami Dolphins.

Irvin said he told defensive tackle Leon Lett after the game he would be "famous forever" for touching the ball after a blocked field goal and allowing the Dolphins a redo of their game-winning kick.

"It was probably my worst game in my NFL career," Irvin laughed. "I must have dropped five or six balls because it was snowing so bad. But nobody remembers that, because Leon Lett slid into that football and made us lose that game."

In addition to his time in the Netflix broadcast booth this season, Irvin has been regularly spotted on the sideline of his alma mater during the Miami Hurricanes' 10-1 start.

The Hurricanes most recently bolstered their playoff hopes with a Saturday win against Virginia Tech, although quarterback Darian Mensah recorded two interceptions while missing star wideout Malachi Toney.

Irvin compared Mensah, who is projected as the No. 9 pick of the 2027 NFL draft on Bleacher Report's latest mock , to Tom Brady when discussing his potential impact in the NFL.

"Tom Brady is a quarterback that is also the emotional leader of the team," Irvin said. "Darian Mensah is a quarterback that's the emotional leader of the team. I give very few quarterbacks higher praise... when you get one that's the emotional leader, you've got something special, and he's something special."

Before the Hurricanes look to solidify their potential playoff spot by closing out the regular season with a Saturday win over Boston College, Irvin will be featured Wednesday on a broadcast team that also includes former NFL stars Nick Foles and Clay Matthews III.

Netflix coverage is scheduled to start at 6 p.m. ET Wednesday before the Thanksgiving Eve matchup between the Packers and Rams kicks off at 8:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase Drops Wild Quote After Brutal Stats, 'Losing When You Know You're Better' is the Worst
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals had their five-game win streak snapped in Monday night's last-second loss to the Washington Commanders, and star receiver Ja'Marr Chase feels his team let one slip away.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals had their five-game win streak snapped in Monday night's last-second loss to the Washington Commanders, and star receiver Ja'Marr Chase feels his team let one slip away.

Chase told reporters after the 22-20 loss on Monday Night Football that the hardest part of accepting defeat was feeling like the Bengals were the better team.

"Losing when you know you're better, I think that's the worst," Chase said (1:05 mark).

The Bengals may have entered Monday night's game as the better team on paper, but they didn't look like it against the Commanders. Chase was held to five catches on nine targets for 31 yards. Cincinnati totaled just 31 rushing yards in the game, failing to support star quarterback Joe Burrow's 300-yard, two-touchdown performance.

Before Monday night's game, The Athletic's Mike Sando reported that multiple executives from other teams view the Bengals as the most dangerous squad in the AFC. Cincinnati will have some work to do if it wants to regain that respect and reach the playoffs for the first time since 2022.

"One loss doesn't determine nothing," Chase said, per Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic. "It's the NFL. You got a loss, you learn from it. We learn from our mistakes. That's what we're going to do. We're going to watch the film, we're going to correct it and move on."

The Bengals (7-3) will try to bounce back when they face the New Orleans Saints (3-7) on Sunday.

articles.title: NFL Panic Meter: Baker Mayfield, who has a $165 million deal, hasn't played well in over a full year
articles.summary: Baker Mayfield had a quiet day Sunday, which has become the norm for him.
articles.body:
There was a contract standoff between Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this summer, which got attention when Mayfield was outspoken over his displeasure. He said it was "very disappointing" that he didn't have an extension, and he felt "disrespected."

The Buccaneers had to be a little worried about paying Mayfield, who is 31 years old, after he played poorly late last season. But they did what most teams do and just paid their quarterback what he wanted. Mayfield got a three-year, $165 million extension with $70 million fully guaranteed upon signing.

And Mayfield has been even worse this season.

Injuries have played a big role. He played through multiple injuries last season, and this season he missed time with a dislocated right thumb and on Sunday he played through a foot injury that had him truly questionable all week. But results are results, and they're not good.

Since Nov. 16 of last season Mayfield has started 15 games. The Buccaneers are 4-11 in those games. That's a team stat, but Mayfield hasn't played well. He has thrown for just 2,610 yards with 15 touchdowns and 13 interceptions for a passer rating of 79. He has just five touchdown passes in seven games this season. His yards per attempt is 6.3, the worst of a career that has included him being traded by the Browns and released by the Panthers after they benched him multiple times. His numbers aren't one of a $55 million quarterback; they're of one who might be benched if he didn't have a $55 million deal.

On Sunday he got to face a Lions defense that was one of the worst in the NFL early in the season and was without linebacker Jack Campbell and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. Mayfield had just 187 yards and 29 came on a final meaningless drive with the Lions leading by 17 points. Mayfield had just one touchdown before he added on a garbage-time touchdown on that drive.

Now what? The Buccaneers can't realistically bench Mayfield after giving him an extension worth $55 million a season, even though undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels showed something when he started for Mayfield earlier this season. They also might have some regrets about giving into pressure on that extension that they were clearly waffling on. Cutting Mayfield before June 1 next year would create a $95.1 million dead cap hit, according to OverTheCap.com . At this point he's not playing up to his contract and hasn't in a long time, but there's not much Tampa Bay can do but stick it out and hope it gets better.

Panic meter: The Bucs should be pretty concerned about that contract, because Mayfield hasn't played well in more than a year. That's not a small sample size.

Metcalf won't be suspended, according to multiple reports, after he was ejected Sunday for seemingly trying to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye. That sounds like great news, until you realize that Metcalf isn't helping the Steelers much when he is on the field.

The Steelers took a big shot on Metcalf with a pricy trade and a big contract. It looked like the Seahawks knew they were getting out at the right time. In 25 games with the Steelers, Metcalf has 1,284 yards and eight touchdowns. This season he's down to 43.4 yards per game. Metcalf has been suspended for or ejected from as many games (three) as he has 100-yard games with Pittsburgh (three). Metcalf will be available to play in Week 12, but it's not like the Steelers should be expecting much.

Panic meter: The Metcalf deal looks like a massive blunder for Pittsburgh.

Can Anthony Richardson Sr. make anything better for Colts?

The Colts are an unserious team. They didn't trade Jonathan Taylor despite good offers, even though he's unlikely to still be in his prime when the Colts are good again. Indianapolis' other trades didn't get nearly the return of similar trades made around the league. They refuse to fire coach Shane Steichen in a lost season, though general manager Chris Ballard was fired earlier this season.

And the release of Daniel Jones, less than 24 hours after he made his 11th straight start to begin the season, provided further evidence that the Colts really don't seem to have a plan. But at least they can finally take a look at Richardson.

Richardson probably isn't going to be an epiphany. His accuracy issues are hard to overcome. But there's no loss in replacing Jones, who ranked 32nd among 32 qualified quarterbacks in EPA per play this season, and at least Indianapolis gets to find out if anything has changed. Richardson did look better in preseason. It would provide at least something good from a miserable season.

Panic meter: Colts fans just want the season to mercifully end.

Minter took over as head coach of a Baltimore Ravens franchise that isn't used to losing. And he has lost a lot of games.

Sunday was the Ravens' sixth straight loss, which dropped the Ravens to 4-7. The quarterback situation has been rough after Lamar Jackson's injury but Baltimore's defense has been a major problem, allowing 32.4 points per game over the last five weeks. Minter is a defensive-minded head coach and that's a bad look.

There's still very little chance Minter is one and done. But this is a franchise that is not used to losing. They've lost double-digit games five times since moving to Baltimore in 1996. They lost 12 games in 1996 and haven't lost more than 11 games since. The Ravens have to go 4-2 to avoid a double-digit loss season. If they have a 1-5 finish and match that 12-loss record, or lose all six and set the record, would Minter be let go? In that worst-case scenario, perhaps. It's too early for one-and-done talk yet, but not too soon for Ravens fans to worry they have the wrong coach.

Panic meter: Let's not worry about Minter being fired yet, but he might want to win a few games down the stretch to be sure.

Was the Cardinals' DC really the problem?

The Arizona Cardinals fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday. Given that the Cardinals were 31st in EPA per play allowed, that's not too surprising. But it also doesn't seem like Rallis was the only problem.

The Cardinals don't have a lot of talent on defense. Arizona doesn't have a single defender that ranks higher than 27th at their position in Pro Football Focus' grades . They have only one player who has more than three sacks, and it's safety Budda Baker with 3.5. Maybe Rallis wasn't helping, but it seems like changing defensive coordinators won't matter if Arizona doesn't find multiple upgrades in personnel over the offseason.

Panic meter: A magician might be needed to help the Cardinals defense become a top 10 unit in 2027.

J.J. McCarthy has settled in as the New York Giants' starter, and his dual-threat ability gives him a reasonable amount of fantasy upside. He barely topped 14 fantasy points against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, but he has a much better matchup this week against the Indianapolis Colts.

Kaelon Black doesn't have the most attractive of matchups this week, as the Seattle Seahawks have surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs. However, the San Francisco 49ers rookie has seen a sizeable workload as Christian McCaffrey's top complement in recent weeks.

Black had just 2.5 fantasy points against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, but he has reached double digits in two of his past four games. He's still rostered in only 44 percent of fantasy leagues.

On Friday, the Steelers will host the Denver Broncos, who have surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends. Freiermuth is still only rostered in 41 percent of fantasy leagues.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Drops Funny Quote on Spiking Ball in Commanders' Win vs. Bengals After Giants Botch
articles.summary: Washington Commanders star quarterback Jayden Daniels refused to make the same mistake twice.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders star quarterback Jayden Daniels refused to make the same mistake twice.

Facing a one-point deficit in the waning seconds of Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals, Daniels connected with Antonio Allen for a 42-yard pass and had to sprint down the field to spike the ball, setting up Drew Stevens' game-winning field goal for a 22-20 victory.

Daniels After Win: 'I Live for These Moments'

The situation conjured up memories of Daniels' botched spike against the New York Giants in overtime in Week 5, which caused that game to end in a 27-27 tie.

After Monday night's win, Daniels joked that it was up to Washington's offensive linemen to get down the field in time for the spike.

"They better bring their ass down there," Daniels said, per The Athletic's David Aldridge . "They've got to sprint. They've got to get their miles per hour up."

If any member of the Commanders' o-line had committed an illegal procedure penalty by jumping as they lined up, there would have been an automatic 10-second runoff that would've ended the game. However, 320-pound left tackle Brandon Coleman, 324-pound left guard Chris Paul, 313-pound center Lucas Patrick, 309-pound right guard Sam Cosmi, and 315-pound right tackle Josh Conerly Jr. all hauled themselves 40 yards down the field in under 10 seconds to execute the spike.

"Our cardio is definitely pushed right there, for sure," Cosmi said. "But we're built for this. We knew the situation. I was happy about the catches. I'll sprint my ass off, anytime."

articles.title: “I want to make sure I can give back to them in any shape..”: How Patrick and Brittany Mahomes are giving people with intellectual disabilities a chance to find their sporting dreams
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have used their platform to support children and communities through charitable work.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have used their platform to support children and communities through charitable work. One such initiative has given people with intellectual disabilities in Lubbock, Texas, a new place to enjoy sports. Support from Patrick's 15 and the Mahomies Foundation helped High Point Village open a junior-size soccer and flag football field, giving residents more opportunities to stay active and prepare for Special Olympics events.The project also carries a fun connection to the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback. High Point Village's fitness coordinator hopes to teach residents how to throw a behind-the-back pass just like Mahomes.How Patrick Mahomes' charitable work brought a new sports field to TexasHigh Point Village opened the 15 and the Mahomies Field at Tankersley Legacy Park on June 26, 2025. The foundation announced the development the following day, confirming its support for the junior-size soccer and flag football facility.The field gives residents, known as Villagers, a dedicated space to practise for Special Olympics events. It also gives them an opportunity to play with friends, improve their fitness and take part in activities with the wider Lubbock community.Fitness Coordinator Joshua Kuhnley explained what the facility could bring to the residents in High Point Village's June 27 announcement. He said, “We are super excited about this field and what it will bring to better the lives and fitness of our Villagers. The field gives us the opportunity to practice for more Special Olympic events, like soccer and flag football. I’m pumped to have soccer matches, teach the Villagers how to bear crawl and how to throw a perfect behind-the-back pass, just like Patrick Mahomes.”The reference to Mahomes adds a personal touch, but the bigger purpose is to help residents enjoy team sports and develop new skills. The field also expands Tankersley Legacy Park, which opened in November 2024 with a walking trail, basketball court, bocce ball court and pickleball courts.Patrick's interest in helping children goes back to the launch of his foundation. During his April 1, 2019 appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, he spoke about the children he wanted to support.“Those kids are the ones that train harder than me by a hundred times every single day, and I want to make sure I can give back to them in any shape and any way in order to give them the resources they need to have an amazing life,” Mahomes said.What Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have said about supporting young peopleBrittany has also spoken about the couple's commitment to helping children. In an October 4, 2023 announcement about their foundation's national partnership with Boys & Girls Clubs of America, she said, “This meaningful partnership will expand opportunities for kids everywhere, and the places that have positively impacted Patrick and me. We are committed to doing all we can to uplift others.”The partnership included a $1.625 million contribution and a multi-year commitment to support the organisation. It also pledged $1,500 for every Patrick Mahomes touchdown during the regular season.The Lubbock project has a personal connection to Patrick, too. He played college football at Texas Tech before becoming one of the NFL's leading quarterbacks. His foundation's support also reflects its continued connection to West Texas.High Point Village began in 2008, founded by parents who wanted better opportunities for their children with special needs. It now runs year-round programmes, summer camps and support services for people with intellectual disabilities.The new field gives its residents more than another place to exercise. They can practise, compete, spend time with friends and enjoy the game together. Mahomes makes his biggest plays in the NFL, but this project gives the Villagers a field where they can create sporting memories of their own.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jeremiah Smith Falls Behind Mestemaker & Carr in New 2027 NFL Mini-Mock Draft by Baumgardner
articles.summary: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith is generally considered the top prospect in the 2027 NFL draft class, but positional need could trump value next spring.
articles.body:
Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith is generally considered the top prospect in the 2027 NFL draft class, but positional need could trump value next spring.

The Athletic's Nick Baumgardner projected the first 10 picks of the draft and had Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker and Notre Dame signal-caller CJ Carr leapfrogging Smith:

NFL Teams That Could Trade Up for Jeremiah Smith 📈

Mestemaker was the first quarterback off the board in Bleacher Report's most recent mock draft from Nov. 11. He went third overall to the Miami Dolphins. Carr, meanwhile, was the No. 26 pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Baumgardner asserted the pair "have started to separate from the pack" at the quarterback position. Texas' Arch Manning continues to be inconsistent, and Dante Moore's final year at Oregon was derailed by a concussion.

Carr in particular has boosted his stock of late. He threw for 848 yards, six touchdowns and two interceptions in the wins over Miami, Boston College and SMU.

Depending on how the 2027 draft order shakes out, the Tennessee Titans and Los Angeles Chargers could be in a very advantageous position.

Tennessee should still have its quarterback of the future in Cam Ward, while Justin Herbert is under contract with L.A. through 2029. Either could have the luxury of making a trade with a QB-needy team.

In Baumgardner's mock, the Titans parlayed the No. 1 pick into Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore and Tennessee defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam. The Chargers, meanwhile, stayed put and had Smith fall into their laps.

As rough as this season has been for Los Angeles in particular, adding the Buckeyes standout would be a good consolation prize.

articles.title: The NFL is taking over Thanksgiving. But how much football is too much football?
articles.summary: The league, so famous for owning Sundays, will broadcast games on five of six days starting on Wednesday.
articles.body:
You know how Thursday's going to go, right? You're going to load up your plate and feast, you're going to take a moment to catch your breath, you're going to dive back in for more, you're going to grab a quick nap, and then after the sun goes down you're going to go back for one more helping.

I'm talking about your NFL diet, of course, but you'll probably do the same thing with turkey, too. And as with turkey leftovers, there'll come a point when you realize that the fifth helping isn't nearly as much fun as the first.

The NFL has honed its Thanksgiving Day slate into a sleek, efficient set-your-oven-timer tradition. You'll watch the Lions, a team that's finally fun to watch instead of being the equivalent of Thanksgiving green bean casserole. You'll watch the inescapable Cowboys, once again almost ready to make a run. And you'll try to stay awake for the evening game. (You will fail.)

It's been this way since 1934 , when the Lions began playing on Thanksgiving; since 1966, when the Cowboys joined them; and since 2006, when the league added the third game. Every year, before a captive holiday audience, these games do numbers ; last year's Chiefs-Cowboys game was the most-watched NFL regular-season game in history .

And now, with Thanksgiving firmly in hand, the NFL is looking to run up the score. Three years ago, the league rolled out a Black Friday game kicking off midafternoon, so you'll have something to watch as you scroll through sale after sale. This year, the Shield is planting the flag on another spot: Thanksgiving Eve.

Traditionally the province of impromptu high school reunions and travel nightmares, the night before Thanksgiving will now host an NFL game. This year, the Packers will play the Rams on Netflix while you're running around trying to see if you bought yams and figuring out how to defrost a frozen-solid 20-pound turkey in just a few hours. And that's just the start of the NFL turkey festivities.

On Thanksgiving Day, the Lions will play the Bears, and then we'll all try to keep our dinner down as the Eagles play the Cowboys. The evening game will feature one of the best matchups of the year — Chiefs-Bills — and Friday, the Broncos will meet the Steelers. (Even though literally any game would do numbers on Thanksgiving, the NFL is showing some mercy. They've stashed Jets-Dolphins — a game more unhealthy than undercooked turkey — on Sunday rather than exposing America to those kinds of toxins on a holiday.)

Is all this football too much football? Depends on how you frame the question.

The holiday football format has held up like few other pop culture traditions in American life, from radio to television to cable to streaming. And it's based on a simple American truth: We would rather do anything than talk to our families.

OK, that's not quite accurate. It's theoretically possible to both watch football and talk to your family. Encouraged, even, considering how quickly family conversations can swing from friendly banter to open hostility. Long-simmering resentments, gossip, political disputes, in-law trouble, questioning of life choices … why throw open the doors to that furnace when everyone can come together and rail on the Cowboys defense?

There are two ways to look at this explosion of holiday football, from both the fan and the economic perspective. For the vast majority of Americans, the NFL's land grab — which also includes Christmas Eve and three games on Christmas Day — means that there are ever fewer hours when the NFL isn't demanding your attention.

As holiday problems go, "too much football" isn't exactly a terrible one. And hey, if that's what gets you through the holidays, no shame whatsoever. But isn't there something to be said for a bit of peace and quiet, too? Maybe sitting by a fire, or catching up with friends and family, or watching an ungrateful Peppermint Patty crash Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving? There are millions of NFL fans whose lives would measurably improve if they weren't tying their emotional state to their team — you know the ones, I don't have to name them — so maybe give that a try for a couple hours?

Which leads to the larger point: the more football we see, the less important each individual game becomes. For now, Mark Cuban's infamous prediction for the NFL — pigs get fat, hogs get slaughtered — still isn't anywhere close to truth; the league continues to fatten up, year after year. Maybe that'll change, maybe the arrow will flatten out instead of continuing to go up and to the right, but it hasn't yet.

But popularity is context-dependent. The NFL is popular in part because of its scarcity; you wouldn't get eight-figure viewership levels for literally every single game if teams played, say, 162 of them in a season. The league, so famous for owning Sundays, will broadcast games on five of six days starting on Wednesday, and if you think the league doesn't have its eye on similar expansions throughout the season, we have a St. Louis Rams jersey to sell you.

The NFL specializes in creating capital-E Events out of thin air. The Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix will boast fanfare literally worthy of a Super Bowl, including a halftime show featuring U2. The five Thanksgiving games will air on five different networks and services — Netflix, Fox, CBS, NBC and Prime — each with its own spectacle, its own flash-and-dazzle to catch and hold your attention through the holiday noise.

We're getting perilously close to old-man-yells-at-turkey-leg territory here, but when everything is a spectacle, nothing is. Thanksgiving dinner — turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, et cetera — is so damn delicious because it comes around only once a year. But every week? Maybe not so much. Sometimes, you don't know how unique something is until it's everywhere.

Enjoy Thanksgiving, friends, and enjoy the football. It'll all be worth watching. Yes, even Cowboys-Eagles.

articles.title: Twenty years ago, Joey Harrington feasted on Lions on Thanksgiving Day
articles.summary: Joey Harrington was the No. 3 overall pick by the Lions in 2002, but was a bust. He came back to Detroit with the Dolphins in 2006, and won.
articles.body:
DETROIT — Maybe Phil Simms' mother really did make a darn good cobbler.

In all likelihood, though, it probably was something else that made the postgame nosh taste so freakin' sweet for Miami Dolphins quarterback Joey Harrington 20 years ago, when he came back to Detroit and beat the Lions on Thanksgiving Day at Ford Field.

The date was Nov. 23, 2006, and Harrington was in his first year with the Dolphins, after the Lions traded away their former first-round pick that spring.

Harrington started the season in Miami as a backup to Daunte Culpepper, but Culpepper got hurt and Harrington got the call. He won three straight starts leading into the Detroit homecoming, then he proceeded to pick apart the Lions, too, throwing for three touchdowns and 213 yards in a 27-10 win over the Lions. He had a passer rating that day of 107.4; his career passer rating was 69.4.

So it certainly was a memorable day for Harrington in Detroit — and for a 16-year-old singer named Taylor Swift who sang the national anthem; whatever happened to her, anyway? — and also one Lions fans would like to forget.

But not Harrington, who had some fun responding to a post on X (formerly Twitter) by the @20YearsAgoSport account earlier this week. The post showed a clip of Harrington doing a postgame interview with CBS's Jim Nantz and Simms. At the end of the interview, Harrington takes a bit of the blackberry cobbler that Simms said was made by his mother.

Harrington quote-tweeted the X post with: "Not gonna lie, this was some of the best cobbler I've ever had." He punctuated that with the laughing tears emoji.

Harrington, now 48, had a turbulent tenure with the Lions, who drafted him third overall in 2002 out of Oregon. He started for the Lions as a rookie, and in 55 starts with Detroit, he had a record of 18-37 in four seasons. He earned the derogatory nickname, "Joey Blue Skies," from Lions fans who didn't appreciate his rosy outlook when talking to the press, especially after losses.

After the Lions signed free-agent quarterbacks Jon Kitna and Josh McCown after the 2005 season, Harrington was traded to the Dolphins in May 2006, ahead of Nick Saban's second (and final) season as a head coach in the NFL. The Dolphins started that season 1-6 before reeling off four straight victories, all with Harrington as the QB, the last one against the Lions — whose game-day staff taunted him by playing, "Piano Man," in warmups that Thanksgiving Day.

The Dolphins won just one more game the rest of the season and finished 6-10, for Saban's only losing season as a head coach at any level.

After the 2006 season, Harrington signed a two-year, $6 million contract with the Atlanta Falcons, but he only made it one season with them. Harrington then played for the New Orleans Saints in 2008, though he didn't appear in any regular-season games, and didn't play in the NFL again after that season.

For his seven-year NFL career, Harrington started 76 games, and he threw for 79 touchdowns and 85 interceptions. He threw for 60 touchdowns and 62 interceptions with the Lions, who in 2005 fired his coach, Steve Mariucci, and in 2008 fired the man who drafted him, general manager Matt Millen.

Journalist Pablo Torre's latest bombshell is how Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid cooks his famous mac and cheese.

Torre uncovered some missing ingredients from what was previously known about Reid's recipe when speaking with former Chiefs offensive lineman Mitchell Schwartz on Tuesday's episode of Pablo Torre Finds Out.

The investigation started with The Athletic's Charles McDonald reporting in March 2018 that Reid had told him his recipe used seven cheese before providing a list of six cheeses along with the note that "5 cheese should b good."
