articles.title: Shannon Sharpe slams DK Metcalf for concerning trend after his ejection against Philadelphia Eagles
articles.summary: DK Metcalf is under fire after being ejected in the Pittsburgh Steelers’ game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Metcalf was ejected after an altercation with...
articles.body:
DK Metcalf is under fire after being ejected in the Pittsburgh Steelers' game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Metcalf was ejected after an altercation with Eagles' star cornerback Cooper DeJean in the third quarter, when he was kicked out of the game after committing two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties.

The first penalty came when Metcalf and DeJean got into a shoving match after a play, and the second came later in the quarter when Metcalf appeared to poke DeJean near the eye after an incomplete pass.

Making matters worse, Metcalf refused to speak to the media after the game and left the stadium before his teammates even got back to the locker room. When he finally spoke to the media on Monday, he denied poking DeJean, claiming he was only trying to talk to him. DeJean said after the game that the poke "just missed" his eye.

The NFL announced that they would not suspend Metcalf for the incident, clearing him to play the Steelers' next game against the Denver Broncos, but he didn't escape intense criticism from Hall of Fame tight end Shannon Sharpe, who slammed him for a lack of accountability.

Shannon Sharpe slams DK Metcalf for his history of avoiding blame

Sharpe went off on Metcalf on his podcast, Night Cap, following his Monday comments. He was frustrated by the wide receiver's running history of not taking accountability for questionable actions throughout his career.

He said, "Still, he didn't take any accountability for what he had done. It was still Cooper DeJean's fault. Remember, he got suspended when he was in Seattle. It was still someone else's fault.

"Until DK accepts accountability, responsibility for his actions, we're going to find ourselves in a very similar situation again. Again. I don't know why he [doesn't want to talk to the media]. Bro, it's a part of it. If you go look at an NFL contract, a part of talking to the media is in that contract. That is in the contract.

"So this notion of you don't have to talk if you don't want to, that is a lie. It is in the contract you have to talk to the media. I don't know why he was like, 'I was just trying to tell him.' Since when is pointing your finger in someone's face how you talk to someone?

"Everybody knows this is what you do to a receiver, especially one of the ones. You say, 'Let's try to hold him without a catch in the first quarter'. Because they're easily agitated and they're going to get frustrated.

"That's what they do. They know they can prod and get DK out of his comfort zone. he's going to lash out. He lashed out because he's not performing how his paycheck should perform. And it's everyone else's fault except his. He doesn't mention all the dropped passes."

DK Metcalf history of incidents in the NFL

Unfortunately for Metcalf, this is the latest in a long list of incidents during his time in the NFL. He leads all NFL players since 2019 with 15 combined flags for unnecessary roughness, unsportsmanlike conduct, and taunting, resulting in over $750,000 in career NFL fines.

Metcalf's most severe punishment came in December 2025 during his first season with Pittsburgh. After grabbing and swiping at Detroit fan Ryan Kennedy in the stands, the NFL suspended him for the final two games of the regular season.

Rumors circulated online that the fan had used a racial slur, which the fan vehemently denied in a press conference, claiming he had only called Metcalf by his legal first name (DeKaylin) while asking for a jersey signature.

The suspension triggered a clause allowing the Steelers to void $45 million in future guarantees.

During his six seasons in Seattle, Metcalf was ejected twice, against Green Bay in 2021 and San Francisco in 2023, and fined multiple times for on-field altercations and taunting. Unless he begins to take some responsibility for his actions moving forward, this list could continue to grow.

articles.title: Projecting the 2026 NFL playoff bracket after Week 11
articles.summary: The NFL postseason picture is shaping up entering a crucial week of football.
articles.body:
The week of Thanksgiving has long served as the appropriate time to get very serious about the approaching NFL playoffs . Eleven weeks of action has provided a decent enough sample size for us all to make judgements about what type of teams are contenders and which are pretenders. This year brings with it an absolute embarrassment of riches as top-tier matchups roll out over a loooooong holiday weekend. The postseason picture will be much clearer after head-to-head tests help sort it out.

But who wants to wait for the games when predictions could be made right now? No one, that's who.

In the hunt: New England Patriots 5-5, Houston Texans 4-6, Baltimore Ravens 4-7

If the season ended today, the NFL would be out a lot of projected revenue. Fans would be irate. And the Chiefs would have to play in a wild card game by virtue of losing a tiebreaker to the Broncos. Patrick Mahomes and company can sit atop the entire conference and in possession of the sole bye if things break right over the next few days. That will require besting Josh Allen and the Bills, but that's something K.C. has been able to do in the past. The Jaguars and Bengals each missed out on golden opportunities in Week 11 and now must hope to maintain their position as division leaders. Neither the Browns or Steelers may be particularly good but no other team is mounting a serious challenge for the final few spots.

In the hunt: Seattle Seahawks 6-4, Los Angeles Rams 6-4, Dallas Cowboys 5-6, Washington Commanders 4-5-1, Tampa Bay Buccaneers/New Orleans Saints/Atlanta Falcons 3-7

Let's call a spade a spade. For as fearsome as the NFC North has been this season, the 49ers look to be head and shoulders over everyone else in the conference. Detroit and Chicago duke it out on Turkey Day for pole position in the uber-competitive division while the Packers and Rams play in a game may very well decide which side gets in and which gets left watching from home. Carolina and New York have managed to get a little breathing room in their respective race but a large group of underacheiving chasers are still very much alive.

So let's go to the proprietary formula we have here in-house at The Big Lead for some clarity on how the rest of the regular season is going to play out and what the final bracket will look like.

Our model yield some interesting projections.

Look, who are we to argue with a machine. But the human eye test has a real problem with the Steelers being projected to win five of their last seven. The Broncos also don't feel like they should be trusted to win their race against the Chiefs. And Detroit catching the Niners? Doesn't feel likely.

That's just what the inputs and outputs say, though.

articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles finally got back in the win column on Sunday.

They snapped a seven-game losing streak with a 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers — their first victory since September — with third-string QB Joe Milton under center.

But it wasn't all hugs and helmet slaps on Philadelphia's sideline.

According to PHLY Sports' E.J. Smith, two members of the Eagles' staff got into a heated skirmish in the third quarter of Sunday's Week 11 win. And it got physical.

Eagles' Clint Hurtt Got Into it With Team Staffer on Sideline

Smith reported that associate head coach and defensive line coach Clint Hurtt went at it with Fernando Noriega, the team's director of player performance and sports science and head strength and conditioning coach, midway through the third quarter.

Noriega was simply doing his job, and it isn't an easy one. During a defensive series he was trying to keep Hurtt from creeping onto the field, and Hurtt reportedly didn't take it well.

Smith stated Hurtt escalated things with a "throat punch." Bleeding Green Nation added that Hurtt turned and appeared to grab Noriega by the throat before the two were separated.

A group of staffers that included Sirianni stepped in to calm things down. The good news is, by the sound of it, nobody is holding a grudge about what happened.

Smith said multiple players laughed off the exchange after the game. He also said Sirianni came over to talk with Hurtt a few minutes later and seemed to laugh it off himself.

And that wasn't even the only fight on Sunday. Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter after two personal fouls from scuffles with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean. In one of them, Metcalf appeared to poke DeJean in the eye.

"I didn't try to poke him in the eye," Metcalf said on Monday.

Clint Hurtt Has Gotten Heated vs. Steelers Before

This isn't the first time Hurtt has made headlines on the sideline against Pittsburgh.

When the Eagles beat the Steelers 27-13 in December 2024, broadcast cameras caught Hurtt and Sirianni in a heated exchange.

Defensive tackle Jalen Carter had just been flagged for unnecessary roughness, and Hurtt stood between Sirianni and Carter as the head coach tried to get to his player.

"And what Clint was saying was, 'Coach, I got it, I've already handled it,'" Sirianni said the next day.

Still, whatever fire Hurtt brought on Sunday seemed to rub off on the players.

The Eagles traded defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars during the bye. Without him, they sacked Aaron Rodgers five times — two of them from Byron Young (Nolan Smith Jr., Jonathan Greenard and Gabe Hall had the others) — and they held Pittsburgh to just 73 rushing yards.

The win was enough to cool Sirianni's hot seat, at least for now. The 3-7 Eagles visit the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day.
